mpu:49684.tagline: Envision your future with clarity and confidence.
mpu:49684.description:
GradFUTURES is the professional development program of the Princeton University Graduate School. Professional development is an intrinsic part of graduate education at Princeton University, broadening the reach and impact of academic training by preparing our students to make transformative contributions within diverse fields of endeavor and to exercise leadership in ways that expand knowledge, accelerate discovery and serve humanity. We empower graduate students through a holistic and integrative model of professional development that enables them to build the skills and competencies, clarity of purpose and multifaceted relationships they need to become leaders within the academic, public and private sectors.
All student events, programs, and resources of the Princeton University Graduate School, including those of GradFUTURES, are open to all Princeton University students, regardless of identity, such as race, sex, ethnicity, national origin, or other protected characteristics.
mpu:49684.goals:
Pillars of GradFUTURES
• Design a cutting-edge professional development model that engages all graduate students and prepares them with the skills and competencies needed for career success across all fields of endeavor.
• Mobilize all stakeholders to build a campus culture that ensures professional development is a transformative part of graduate education.
• Create bespoke academic, community and industry partnerships to deliver and scale professional development and experiential learning (especially within the innovation ecosystem).
• Leverage Princeton's intellectual capital and alumni networks to deliver lifelong learning and mentorship while deepening graduate alumni affinity.
• Utilize quantitative and qualitative data to share outcomes and demonstrate the impact of a holistic approach to graduate student professional development.

mpu:52695.description: ODUS creates an engaging environment that inspires students to realize their full potential through self-discovery, connection to community, meaningful work, a love of learning, and a life of purpose. ODUS works to enrich the co-curricular experience by cultivating in our students the capacity for responsible citizenship and effective leadership and by promoting the well-being of self and others while upholding the values of integrity, respect, and inclusion that will prepare them for service and success in a global society.

mpu:52878.description:
The Center for Jewish Life embraces all Jewish students, amplifying connections to Jewish meaning, experience, and community. We aspire to provide insights and pathways to help Princeton Jewish students live their lives as a sacred gift. We hope to help every student find their own voice within the larger narrative of the Jewish people – on their own terms – at their own level -but in ways that are deeply connected to the wisdom of our ancient tradition and linked to the opportunities and challenges of today’s complex world.
Our mission is to cultivate friendship and Jewish community, inspire and nurture personal paths to Jewish identity, empower and mentor Jewish students, explore Life’s Big Questions, and promote well-being and happiness. Our values are to be welcoming and inclusive, nurturing and inspiring, vibrant and celebratory, innovative and student driven. With the launch of our new Strategic Plan, we are working towards a vision where every Jewish student at Princeton takes advantage of Jewish opportunities that are personally and intellectually engaging in the spirit of the overall Princeton experience.

mpu:52941.description:
ACM, the Association for Computing Machinery, is an organization dedicated to fostering communities of people interested in computer science and related interests.
We host an annual competitive programming contest in the fall: Princeton's Computer Science Contest (COSCON), where we have problems from all sects of computer science, such as machine learning, systems, algorithms, cryptography, and more! We also host weekly reading groups on topics such as Natural Language Processing, Computer Vision, Systems, and more!
We also send multiple teams to ICPC, the International Collegiate Programming Contest. Check us out at https://princeton.acm.org
mpu:52941.whatWeDo: Members get exclusive access to our newsletter, our Code@Night events and other career-related news and information.
mpu:52941.goals: Our primary goal is to spread our love for Computer Science among the Princeton student body.

mpu:52942.description:
Home to all people of African descent: from the continent and the diaspora! Through our programming, we strive to offer a space where we can all “breathe, dream, and live Africa together.”
This organization is open to all Princeton University students interested in supporting our organization’s mission, regardless of identity, such as race, sex, ethnicity, national origin, or other protected characteristics.

mpu:52945.description:
Princeton's first, premier, and only late-night talk show, presenting 6 episodes per year in Frist Theater. Presenting Season 15, hosted by Jack Goodman '27 and co-hosted by Jack Musser '27.
Instagram: @allnighterpton
YouTube: @AllNighterPrinceton
mpu:52945.whatWeDo: Reach out to us to learn more about getting involved as a writer, actor, technician, house band member, or talent guest! We pride ourselves on engaging with as much of the campus community as possible, and have a revolving door of contributing actors and guests each episode.

mpu:52946.description: We are a community of left-wing Jewish Princetonians who are committed to ending Israeli occupation and apartheid and ensuring safety and freedom for all in Israel-Palestine and in the world. Our own history of oppression compels us to call on individuals, institutions, and leaders—particularly in the Jewish community—to condemn Israeli apartheid and all forms of injustice. We gather for Shabbat dinners, holiday celebrations, text studies, speaker events, vigils, and rallies. All are welcome.
mpu:52946.goals:
Justice for All
We are committed to working towards social justice, freedom, and dignity for all people. We stand in solidarity with oppressed groups, including immigrants, Muslims, people of color, indigenous peoples, LGBTQIA-identifying people, and poor people, and we commit ourselves to faithful alliance and collaboration with communities in need.
Commitment to Jewish Heritage
While we represent a range of Jewish backgrounds and ideologies, we share a deep respect and love for Jewish history, text, and community. Our Jewish tradition compels us to help build a more just and free future for all, and we rely on our ancestors’ teachings to sustain and guide us in this work.
Listening & Learning
We recognize how little we know and celebrate opportunities to learn from each other, from our heritage, and from our allies. We are committed to studying the issues that are most important to us and we encourage free and open discourse -- even with those who disagree with us.
Building Warm Community
We work to be a welcoming space for progressive Jewish Princetonians of all abilities, ages, backgrounds, classes, genders, races, and sexualities. Through our differences, we aim to cultivate an environment of respect, friendship, and joy in our community.
Accountability & Transparency
We recognize that this work may be difficult. While emphasizing compassion, we hold ourselves accountable for our actions and their effects on others. As such, we are committed to transparency and honest communication.

mpu:52947.description: To create a supportive and collaborative community of chemical engineers on campus, get students involved with the department, faculty, and researchers, and prepare and inspire students to be chemical engineers after Princeton

mpu:52948.tagline: Supporting and fostering a community of budding scientists interested in research and clinical work
mpu:52948.description:
The Princeton Physician Scientists Society (PPSS) is a student organization dedicated to supporting Princeton students interested in pursuing careers that integrate medicine, scientific research, or both. We seek to build a community for students interested in physician-scientist and MD/PhD pathways while providing opportunities for mentorship, professional development, and exploration of careers at the intersection of clinical medicine and biomedical research.
Throughout the year, we invite physician-scientists, MD/PhD students, researchers, and other members of the medical and scientific communities to speak with Princeton students about their research, training, and career paths. We also organize opportunities for students to connect with peers, alumni, and professionals who can provide guidance as they explore careers in medicine and research.
mpu:52948.whatWeDo:
* A supportive community of Princeton students and alumni interested in pursuing careers in medicine, scientific research, or physician-scientist careers.
* Opportunities to hear from and connect with physician-scientists, MD/PhD students, researchers, and other professionals.
* Access to journal clubs, alumni panels, networking opportunities, and information sessions about research careers and applying to MD/PhD programs.
* Opportunities to learn about different pathways for combining clinical practice with scientific research.
mpu:52948.goals: To support and foster a community of Princeton students interested in integrating medicine and scientific research, while providing mentorship, educational programming, and opportunities to explore physician-scientist and related career paths.

mpu:52950.description: To promote and encourage, amongst its members, a collaborative environment to explore the realm of anime, manga, visual novels, and other forms of Japanese and general East Asian media forms.

mpu:52951.description:
We aim to foster an atmosphere where sex is dignified, respectful, and beautiful; where human relationships are affirming and supportive; where marriage is given pride of place among those relationships; where motherhood and authentic femininity are reverenced; where true masculinity and committed fatherhood are vital to family life; and where no one is objectified, instrumentalized, or demeaned.
We hope to provide those students who strive to understand, live, and love their commitment to chastity and ‘traditional’ sexual and familial ethics with the support they need to make their time at Princeton the best it can be.
Lastly, we wish to offer these values to the wider Princeton community and promote a culture of charitable dialogue and mutual understanding among all Princetonians.

mpu:52952.description:
The South West Asian and North African (SWANA) Society shares our culture through comedy, music, film, food, and activism.
This organization is open to all Princeton University students interested in supporting our organization’s mission, regardless of identity, such as race, sex, ethnicity, national origin, or other protected characteristics.

mpu:52954.description: The Princeton Armenian Society strives to create a safe and rewarding community space for its members through a variety of cultural, social, and activist events across the Princeton community.
mpu:52954.goals: Our goal is to represent the unified voice of our members and provide a space on campus for Armenian-American Princeton students to connect with their roots and with one another and be engaged with the community as a whole.

mpu:52955.description: A place for you to enjoy art!

mpu:52956.description: Princeton's Asian American Student Association was founded in 1970 with the intent to bring together students of Asian American descent. As the largest affinity group on campus, we co-sponsor several speaker events, discuss APIDA issues, engage with political activism, serve our surrounding community, and host social events.

mpu:52957.description:
The Princeton Association of Black Women seeks to create a space of belonging and provide a community for Black women at Princeton University. By uniting current and former Princeton Black women*, PABW aspires to foster a sisterhood that promotes academic excellence, community awareness, and allyship in addition to social, emotional and professional support during and after our time at Princeton.
*PABW aims to include all individuals including those who identify as genderqueer, nonconforming, or transgender.

mpu:52960.description:
Princeton Autonomous Vehicle Engineering (PAVE) is a Princeton University student research organization focused on the advancement of robotics and artificial intelligence. For the past 20 years, the team has focused on conducting research and engaging in competitive challenges with a variety of land and maritime vehicles. PAVE's work is highly impact-focused, emphasizing the development of novel techniques and algorithms.
During the 2026 / 2027 academic year, PAVE will begin to work on adding a new autonomous system to a Mercedes Benz test vehicle from the Princeton Computational Imaging Labs. This system will implement sensor, compute, and control capabilities developed by our organization.
The team is open to students of all skill levels.

mpu:52962.description:
Princeton University Ballet, founded in 2008, is an entirely student-led, innovative, and evolving ballet company. The company creates and performs two shows a year, showcasing both student and guest choreography. We strive to renew the expression of ballet while maintaining a strong classical base.
​As members of both a diverse university community and a traditionally restrictive art form, we commit to the pursuit of a more inclusive environment. Our distinct position as a company of student artists promotes agency and collaboration that reinvigorates a love of dance among members.

mpu:52963.description:
The Princeton University Band exists primarily for the enjoyment of its members and for the entertainment of the University community.
This organization is open to all Princeton University students interested in supporting our organization’s mission, regardless of identity, such as race, sex, ethnicity, national origin, or other protected characteristics.
mpu:52963.whatWeDo: A fun and welcoming environment for all! If you don't know how to play a musical instrument, we are happy to teach you. We also provide all necessary instruments at zero cost to members. We go on fun trips to away sports games, again at no cost to members.

mpu:52965.description: The Bee Team's mission is to foster a campus-wide conversation about bee conservation through taking care of our two beehives in the greenhouse.
mpu:52965.whatWeDo: Members receive hands on experience working with bees and can partake in related events like honey collection.
mpu:52965.goals: The Bee Team's goal is to expose the Princeton community to the wonders of beekeeping.

mpu:52967.description: Princeton Bhangra is dedicated to preserving and promoting the vibrant and energetic tradition of Bhangra, a folk dance from Punjab, through passionate performance and cultural education. Our mission is to foster a sense of community and cultural pride within our team and the broader Princeton community, while inspiring audiences with the rich heritage and joyful spirit of Bhangra. We strive to be ambassadors of diversity, inclusivity, and artistic excellence, celebrating Punjabi culture while embracing creativity and innovation in our performances.

mpu:52969.description: The Black Arts Company is a dance group that seeks to share and embrace different genres of hip hop and celebrate the history behind many Black artists and creatives. Additionally, the Black Arts Company serves as an affinity space for Black students on campus, also welcoming those who wish to share their appreciation for the culture.

mpu:52971.tagline: An inclusive community created for Black Premeds by Black Premeds
mpu:52971.description: Black Pre-Medical Society of Princeton University seeks to empower the Black pre-medical community to tackle the unique issues that face underrepresented students in medicine, cultivate long-lasting connections between Black pre-med students, address community health challenges affecting the Black community, and provide the necessary support and resources catered to the specific needs of Black students as they ascend to medical school.

mpu:52972.description: The purpose of the Black Student Union is to promote and sustain an atmosphere that is conducive to the political, cultural, social, professional, and educational growth and success of the African diasporic community as well as foster a sense of community among black students at Princeton. Such an atmosphere and community can be best achieved and sustained through the pursuit, discussion, and application of knowledge, proactive leadership, and social, political and cultural engagement within the Black community. The Black Student Union does not represent a shared political ideology, but rather a shared experience and/or concern with the Black experience at Princeton University.

mpu:52974.description: BodyHype Dance Co. is an eclectic, innovative, and HYPE family of dancers, choreographers, and multimedia creatives. We aim to produce a professional caliber of dance in an environment that centers artistic possibility, and to constantly push the boundaries of what dance can be. BodyHype is deeply committed to cultivating a diverse, equitable, and inclusive community, respecting all styles of dance, and supporting each other both within and outside of the studio.

mpu:52976.description: To promote awareness of Brazilian culture and foster a sense of community among Brazilian students!

mpu:52977.description: Develop a competitive bridge team and participate in intercollegiate tournaments. This organization is open to all Princeton University students interested in supporting our organization’s mission, regardless of identity, such as race, sex, ethnicity, national origin, or other protected characteristics.

mpu:52980.description: Business Today is an undergraduate-focused business organization based at Princeton University. Business Today’s team of Princeton undergraduates and board of alumni trustees are singularly focused on expanding the opportunities for communication for today’s undergraduate leaders. Currently, Business Today achieves this mission through three multi-day conferences, an on-campus seminar series, a national magazine, an online multimedia platform, and many other assorted programs. A 501(c)(3) nonprofit organization, Business Today is committed to creating the best experience and most value for all conference attendees, content consumers, and organization members. Business Today is open to all Princeton University students interested in supporting our organization’s mission, regardless of identity, such as race, sex, ethnicity, national origin, or other protected characteristics.

mpu:52981.description: Princeton Canadians create community for students from or interested in Canada and Canadian culture.

mpu:52982.description: PCC (n): A vibrant community for students from the Caribbean and its diasporas that celebrates and upholds Caribbean culture at Princeton!☀️

mpu:52983.description: Since its inception, CABAM has been working tirelessly to bring the Princeton University community only the finest cheeses... and the worst movies. Highlights from the past have included classics like The Room, forgotten gems like the 1990 Captain America movie, and even a marathon of Neil Breen's truly singular filmography.

mpu:52984.description: We host weekly casual chess meetups and organize a few chess competitions and trainings every year.

mpu:52985.description: We are child's play improv, a group of students united by our love of improv comedy! We aim to make improv fun and accessible to everyone, regardless of their experience level.
mpu:52985.whatWeDo:
Child’s Play is Princeton’s youngest improv group! The institution of Child’s Play, unlike other Princeton improv groups, can’t legally drink, drive, or have acne, but we DO know how to have amazing, mirthful, totally unscripted fun.
Everyone knows how to have fun! Child’s Play doesn’t believe that improv is an elite and unattainable skill. We want to keep it weird. Surprising. Spunky. Spontaneous. We want genuine. We want you, because that’s where it all comes from! We are our own wildest and most wonderful creations. Go ahead and jot that down.
So you don’t need improv experience, a friend who’s a theater kid, or the word “zany” in your vocabulary. You don’t even have to be part of our group! As part of our goal to make improv more diverse and accessible, Child’s Play holds open workshops every other month. Anyone, and we mean anyone, can be a part of our family. We just want you to be bold, confident, and open-minded…the rest, as they say, is child’s play.
mpu:52985.goals: We hope to make improvisational comedy as diverse, accessible, and enjoyable as possible, both within the structure of our extremely beginner-friendly group and within the Princeton community at large. To this end, we would like to share the gift of improv comedy as an activity and encourage newcomers to try it out. We would like to demonstrate that everyone has the ability to be a successful improviser and push people to be curious and proactive about exploring improvisation, instead of shying away from it as an intimidating activity. We also want our performances to be fun and spark joy.

mpu:52987.description:
Princeton Chinese Students Association celebrates Chinese culture and fosters an inclusive community by creating opportunities for students to connect, learn, and engage through cultural and social events throughout the year.
Connect with us:
Instagram: @csaprinceton
Email: csa.princeton@gmail.com

mpu:52988.description: Princeton Chinese Theatre (PCT) was founded in April 2008 by five sophomores and one junior Chinese stage play enthusiasts. The theater group is run entirely by students, from publicity to technical support, from directing to acting, while receiving professional guidance at the same time. We aim at promoting Chinese language and culture by performing Chinese stage plays mostly in Mandarin, both on campus and outside the University. Each year, PCT puts on two shows, one in fall and one in spring, while hosting other activities along the course of the year.
mpu:52988.goals: Our recent productions include 平原上的摩西 (A Burning Christmas, 2025 Fall at Whitman Theater), 恋爱的犀牛 (Rhinoceros in Love, 2026 Spring at Frist Theater), 红岸往事 (Echos From the Red Coast, 2025 Spring at Frist Theatre), and Chinglish (2024 Fall at Whitman Theatre).

mpu:52994.description: The Princeton College Democrats represent the Democratic Party at Princeton University. As such, we work to support both Democratic ideals and candidates. We seek to advance liberalism among our fellow students at all levels of government, from local to federal. Together, we span the ideological range of the Democratic Party, from Blue Dog Moderates to Democratic Socialists.

mpu:52995.description: Founded in 1898, Princeton College Republicans is one of the oldest and largest Republican clubs in America and represents the GOP at Princeton University. We work to support the RNC, NRCC, NRSC, and NJGOP. Our alumni include John Foster Dulles, Jeff Sessions, Samuel Alito, and Ted Cruz. Our mission is to engage and empower students to actively participate in the democratic process through education and advocacy. By building strong connections with like-minded organizations, we seek to strengthen our impact and influence. Ultimately, we strive to create a dynamic environment where conservative ideas can be explored, debated, and advanced.

mpu:52998.description: The Princeton Undergraduate Composers Collective is a student-run group dedicated to music composition. Our members come from many different musical backgrounds with varying levels of experience with music composition. Even if you have never composed before, you are more than welcome to join us, and all styles of music are welcome!

mpu:52999.description:
Princeton Conservation Society (PCS) is Princeton University’s home on campus for all things environmental, wildlife conservation, and biology/life sciences. Throughout the academic year, we host events on- and off-campus open to the entire University community, from guest speaker events to local forest restoration, from whale watching on the New Jersey coast to trips around the world (Indonesia, Panama, e.g.). Between tree plantings, invasive species removals, and trail maintenance, we do our part in serving partner needs while getting our hands dirty. Our overarching goal is to promote education and enact action on today’s numerous environmental issues. We prioritize making wildlife conservation a more accessible and diverse opportunity than it’s known to be.
Our organization is fully student-run under the Office of the Dean of Undergraduate Students (ODUS), and we are graciously supported by various departments on campus.
mpu:52999.whatWeDo: An amazing community of nature and life lovers!
mpu:52999.goals: Learn about nature, ecology, wildlife management, environmental policy, and work together with communities to foster belonging for people and animals.

mpu:53001.description: We provide a hub for twisty puzzle enthusiasts and competitors to learn and build community!

mpu:53003.description: PDP is Princeton’s only competitive debate team and one of the most competitively successful debating societies in the world. In the last few years, we have been National Champions, North American Champions, and World Championship Runner-ups. We travel all over the country and the world every year, from Boston and San Francisco to Seoul and London (all on Princeton’s dime).

mpu:53004.description: Decem is dedicated to promoting and encouraging amongst its members a profound appreciation of choral music, and a desire to share its qualities with the Princeton community. Furthermore, we desire that the members might cultivate a supportive and open-minded artistic environment, dedicated to promoting the creation of music at the highest level.

mpu:53005.description:
diSiac Dance Company was founded at Princeton University in 1998, and has since become one of the largest and most distinguished student-run dance companies on campus.
diSiac’s primary styles are contemporary and hip-hop, but we explore almost everything in between, from heels and jazz to house and popping. We seek to understand and respect the history and culture of the dance forms we engage with, but nevertheless strive to push the limits of movement beyond categorization. Our dancers range from having no experience at all to coming from pre-professional backgrounds at companies and studios such as Juilliard, Nederlands Dans Theater, Millennium Dance Complex, Urban Dance Camp, Alvin Ailey Dance Theater, Ballet Austin, and Hubbard Street.
In a typical year, we put on two major shows, perform at numerous campus events, host workshop series (with guest workshops from top choreographers in NYC), and execute innovative creative projects (including a strategic partnership with Lululemon). We partner annually with Princeton’s Best Buddies, BigSibs, Trenton Youth Dancers, and CityStep volunteer programs, and are working to further expand our community outreach beyond the University’s campus.
Our motto states, “You think you know, but you have no idea,” to convey that the possibilities for artistic and personal growth within our blue family are endless. The relationships formed between members make this group the one-of-a-kind, lifelong experience that it is. diSiac is so much more than an elite dance company–we are an incredible family, social group, and support network that lasts long beyond our years at Princeton. APHRO!!!

mpu:53006.description: DoroBucci is Princeton University’s premier African dance company grounded in a mission to use dance as a medium to uplift, celebrate and promote a deeper understanding and appreciation for African culture. Since its founding in 2015, DoroBucci has grown significantly, embracing and uplifting the beautiful diversity of people from the African continent and the entire diaspora. DoroBucci endeavors to cultivate an inclusive community that exists at the intersection of artistic innovation and cultural expression.

mpu:53009.description: HackPrinceton is one of the original student-run hackathons, tracing back to 2010, and HackPrinceton’s legacy is well known and respected amongst the hacker community. The primary mission of HackPrinceton is to create an inclusive environment and provide resources for students from all backgrounds to pursue interesting projects, learn new technologies and programming skills, and meet awesome people.
mpu:53009.whatWeDo: Members have the opportunity to plan an event catering to hundreds of people and connect with industry leaders and various companies.
mpu:53009.goals: HackPrinceton's goals are to plan and host an amazing hackathon to empower students to learn and pursue interesting projects in an inclusive environment.

mpu:53010.description: Forging the next generation of technical engineers and founders through the intersection of gaming, strategy, programming, and artificial intelligence.

mpu:53013.description: Ellipses Slam Poetry is Princeton's oldest spoken word group. We are dedicated to creating a community of poets who write, workshop, and perform together.

mpu:53014.tagline: Princeton University Energy Association (PUEA) is the only student group on campus dedicated to exploring the energy field from every approach imaginable.
mpu:53014.description:
Princeton University Energy Association (PUEA) is the only student group on campus dedicated to exploring the energy field from every approach imaginable.
Run entirely by undergraduate students from both STEM and humanities/social sciences, we bring exciting opportunities every week for students on campus to meet and learn from energy experts, executives, and scholars, and participate in energy-related tours, conferences, and community service.
Current opportunities for members include weekly dinners with professors and alumni, frequent socials, planning and/or attending our annual conference, and engaging with alumni and the campus community through our publication team.

mpu:53015.description:
The Undergraduate Engineering Council
1. Organizes and hosts the annual SEAS Teaching Awards ceremony
2. Act as a liaison between engineering students and faculty
3. Plans community-building study breaks
4. Provides guidance to freshmen new to the engineering program

mpu:53016.description: Founded in 1999, the Princeton Entrepreneurship Club (E-Club) is an entirely student-run organization that aims to foster student entrepreneurship at Princeton. Our 17 operational subteams engage the most visionary Princeton students to drive worldwide innovation and impact. As the largest club on campus, we have over 400 members and reach more than 3,000 students through our events.
mpu:53016.whatWeDo:
- Join a diverse community on campus, full of passionate, entrepreneurial, and welcoming individuals that you can call family
- Professional Opportunities, Networking Opportunities, Social Events, Access to E-Club Alumni
- Further your passions and make an impact, both on and off campus!

mpu:53017.description: We empower current and future global leaders to pursue the prudent advancement of social and scientific policy, systems, and technologies, for a brighter future.

mpu:53020.description:
eXpressions Dance Company is a student-run group of artists who shares yearly performances, collaborations with performing arts groups, and open workshops with the Princeton community. Through these opportunities, we:
- develop an authentic and personal exploration of choreography and movement.
create a space for sharing diverse perspectives on dance, fostering leadership skills, and building valuable relationships with peer mentors.
- dedicate ourselves to cultivating lasting friendships and a close community through our shared passion for dance.

mpu:53021.description: We are a student run organization that collaborated with the Office of Sustainability and Office of Community and Regional Affairs to plan an on campus Farmers Market. We work on vendor outreach, and marketing through collaboration with other student groups. The market is environmentally focused and works to support local NJ farms and small businesses.

mpu:53022.tagline: Princeton's premier publication for science fiction, fantasy, horror, and speculative fiction
mpu:53022.description: figments is Princeton University’s premier publication for science fiction, fantasy, horror, and speculative fiction. Find our previous issues and more information at figments.princeton.edu!
mpu:53022.goals: We aim to harness the imaginations of Princeton students and alumni, and provide a space to publish the most outlandish and wonderful stories that they can produce. We believe that speculative and genre fiction as literary forms are powerful, and we work to develop their presence on Princeton’s campus.

mpu:53023.description: Founded in 2023, Princeton Pictures is Princeton University's only filmmaking club, with the mission to unite aspiring filmmakers and create visual stories that will have a lasting impact. Through hands-on experience, collaboration, and education, we aim to equip our members with the knowledge, skills, and resources to create impactful and innovative films.

mpu:53027.description: The Footnotes have been bringing fresh, low-voice A Cappella to Princeton's campus since 1959. We perform a repertoire that includes popular, jazzy, and original compositions both domestically and internationally each year. Beyond Princeton's campus, we aim to spread the joy of music to students of all ages through performances and workshops. Most of all, we are a space for singers from all backgrounds to perform at a high level while forming friendships that last a lifetime.

mpu:53029.description:
Fuzzy Dice, Princeton's (Self-Proclaimed) Most Attractive Improv Group, was founded in 2004 as the first troupe on campus to offer both long- and short-form improv comedy. Since then, we have performed at campuses and theaters across the US. Fuzzy Dice is both an improv group and a family, which makes it that much easier for us to enjoy doing what we love.
www.fuzzydiceimprov.com

mpu:53030.description: The Princeton University Geoscience Society (PUGS) is an open-to-all group for those interested in earth sciences, from the planet's atmosphere down to its core. Within the group, we encourage a mingling of everything in between, which will allow us more-thoroughly to understand our planet and its dynamics. We engage in many activities that bond us over our common interest, including occasional trips, workshops, and general meetings.

mpu:53033.description: Princeton University Gospel Ensemble is a ministry started in 1971 that, compelled by Jesus' love & our love for Him, courageously and communally pursues and proclaims God's peace. We are a student-led choir open to all that spreads the light of Jesus Christ to the Princeton campus and local community through music. Our repertoire includes a variety of traditional spirituals, hymns, and upbeat contemporary gospel music. This organization is open to all Princeton University students interested in supporting our organization’s mission, regardless of identity, such as race, sex, ethnicity, national origin, or other protected characteristics.
mpu:53033.goals: Facilitate a community on campus that loves God and is committed to spreading his message of truth through song.

mpu:53039.description: Hoagie Club aims to change how we build campus applications and establish a proper software engineering culture around them. We want to turn Princeton applications from a bunch of isolated side-projects into an integrated software system. We aim to emulate industry-style software engineering and project management.
mpu:53039.whatWeDo: Access to meaningful web application design and development projects and more.
mpu:53039.goals: Instead of a competitive and stressful “hero” culture, we strive to build each other up and learn from one another. Together we’ll continue to explore what lessons and meaningful experiences creating cool apps together can teach us.

mpu:53040.description: To foster cultural exchange, unity, and support among students while celebrating and promoting the rich heritage of Hong Kong.

mpu:53049.description: The IRC aims to provide a forum for free and open debate and discussion in international affairs.

mpu:53050.description: J Street U Princeton is the campus home for Pro-Peace, Pro-Israel, and Pro-Palestine students; and one of 60 J Street U chapters nationwide. We work to engage Princeton students in meaningful conversations around the Israeli-Palestinian conflict and to organize Princetonians to advocate for strong American leadership toward a negotiated resolution to the conflict and an end to the occupation.

mpu:53051.description: As an organization, J-Lats has four main pillars. Firstly, we will serve as a platform to form connections within the Jewish Latinx community. Most members of the Jewish-Latinx community do not know each other due to the lack of a unifying organization that connects them. Secondly, we will strive to bridge the Latinx and Jewish community on Princeton’s campus. Recently, these two communities have not collaborated nor interacted with one and other. Our goal is to serve as a unifying force between these two groups. Thirdly, we will highlight the diversity of the Jewish and Latinx community to the Princeton community. There are a myriad of stereotypes surrounding Judaism and Latinidad that J-Lats will effectively combat through its existence and programming opportunities for the student body. By celebrating the inherent diversity embedded within Judaism and Latinidad, we will expose the Princeton community to this reality. Lastly, J-Lats will offer community engagement opportunities with both the Jewish and Latinx community on and off campus to address the needs of community patterns and educate about Jewish-Latinx culture.

mpu:53052.description:
JSA hosts events involving Japanese culture. Anyone interested is welcome to any of our events!
* This organization is open to all Princeton University students interested in supporting our organization's mission, regardless of identity, such as race, sex, ethnicity, national origin, or other protected characteristics.

mpu:53057.description: The Princeton Katzenjammers, the oldest mixed-voice acapella group in the country, seeks to bring the sounds of jazz, theatre classics, and more to the Princeton community and beyond.

mpu:53058.description: Kindred Spirit was founded in 1991 by Dee Hausman in response to a vision God had placed in her heart to begin a Christian a cappella group on Princeton’s campus. Since then, KS has been offering inspirational outreach to the Princeton community and to our audiences everywhere through fellowship, arch sings, gospel jams, community service, and shared testimonies.
mpu:53058.goals: We are devoted to spreading the gospel through song, to encouraging one another as brothers and sisters in Christ, and to glorifying the name of Jesus Christ.

mpu:53059.description: Koleinu is Princeton's oldest and only Jewish a cappella group.
mpu:53059.goals: We sing a mix of traditional Jewish music along with modern Israeli and American pop music.

mpu:53060.description: The mission of KSAP at Princeton is to host events and provide support for Korean international, Korean-American, and Korean-interest students. KSAP also aims to offer Koreans a place to network with others and find a community here at Princeton. KSAP seeks to accomplish such a mission by hosting cultural, professional, and academic events.

mpu:53062.description: The mission of La Vie En Cello is to unite a group of cellists at Princeton with the shared goal of spreading our passion for music.

mpu:53064.description: LEM fosters the Latine Community at Princeton who have an interest in healthcare, Latine care, and medicine. LEM is part of a national organization called the Latino Medical Student Association. Its purpose is to acknowledge the health needs of the Latine community, as well as to promote the interests and support of Latine undergraduate students interested in careers in healthcare or medicine.

mpu:53070.description:
Liars' Club is for all who want to have fun playing social deduction games with lies and trickery.
Our regular games include One Night Ultimate Werewolf, Avalon, Coup, and Blood on the Clocktower.
There is no time commitment at all, so come and leave when you want.
This organization is open to all Princeton University students interested in supporting our organization’s mission, regardless of identity, such as race, sex, ethnicity, national origin, or other protected characteristics.

mpu:53074.description:
MTG Club seeks to provide a fun, inclusive environment for Magic the Gathering at Princeton by supporting both new and existing players across many game formats.
This organization is open to all Princeton University students interested in supporting our organization’s mission, regardless of identity, such as race, sex, ethnicity, national origin, or other protected characteristics.
mpu:53074.goals: See the mission statement. Due note that this organization is open to all Princeton University students interested in supporting our organization’s mission, regardless of identity, such as race, sex, ethnicity, national origin, or other protected characteristics

mpu:53077.description: The Malaysian and Singaporean Association builds community for Malaysian and Singaporean students and shares our cultures with the broader campus community through our events.

mpu:53078.description:
Más Flow is Princeton's premier Latin dance company that is home to 50+ members from diverse backgrounds and a wide range of dance experience. Founded in 2013, Más Flow is a relatively new dance company on campus that is growing in popularity and size!
Our primary dance styles are salsa, reggaeton, and bachata but we also explore other Latin dance styles such as merengue, Brazilian Funk, and Folklorico. As Princeton's ONLY Latin dance company on campus, we hope to spread an appreciation and love for Latin culture through music and dance to the Princeton community. During a typical school year, Más Flow hosts several social events in BlackBox to gather the Princeton community for a night of Latin music and dance! In addition to socials, we also host one major show during the Spring Semester and guest perform for other dance companies.
In efforts to remain active in our local community, Más Flow is hosting several dance workshops for Princeton undergraduate and graduate students. We have also recently partnered with the Trenton Youth Dancers and Foundation Academies (a charter school in Trenton) to host workshop classes for students outside of the University's campus.
Although Más Flow is primarily a dance company, our members also spend a lot of time together outside of rehearsals. From studying in Frist to sharing meals and hosting annual holiday company dinners and cast parties, Más Flow hopes to foster a welcoming and loving community for all its members. We can't wait to chat with you soon! DAME MAS DAME DAME DAME MAS FLOWW.

mpu:53079.description: As Muslims Advocates for Social Justice, we aim to amplify the voices of underserved communities and to address local and global issues. We focus on education, advocacy, and service as ways we can take more active roles in our communities.

mpu:53080.description:
PUMRS is an active club with ties to the Princeton Materials Institute that sponsors workshops, course advising and nerdy fun. We are also a great resource for those considering a Materials Science and Engineering Minor.
This organization is open to all Princeton University students interested in supporting our organization’s mission, regardless of identity, such as race, sex, ethnicity, national origin, or other protected characteristics.

mpu:53081.description:
Welcome to Princeton Math Club!! We host a variety of math-related events and extravaganzas including colloquia given by mathematics faculty, board game nights, course advising sessions, and our annual in-house competition for 400+ high school students (PUMaC).
All are welcome to join our club listserv, NULLSET, where we communicate all club- and event-related information. If you would like to be added, please email Julian Shah (js7941@princeton.edu).

mpu:53085.description: Princeton Mock Trial is one of the top student-run mock trial programs in the country. We field four teams that compete in tournaments across the country, welcoming undergraduates from all majors and backgrounds. Whether you love theater, legal thinking, or the heat of the competition, there's a place for you on the team! PMT holds tryouts every fall and also runs the premier Training Seminar and Moot Court tournament for high school students to simulate appellate argument.

mpu:53086.tagline: The Nation's Premier Civics Education Program for High School Students, since 1982.
mpu:53086.description:
Princeton Model Congress is the oldest model congress in America. Its inaugural conference took place in 1982 in New York City under the leadership of a group of students from the American Whig-Cliosophic Society, which is the oldest debate union in the country. Over the course of the last three decades, our annual conference has evolved, expanded, and relocated to our nation’s capital Washington, DC to enrich our participants’ experience with an added dimension of realism that no other model congress in America offers.
Princeton Model Congress exemplifies the University’s motto: “In the nation’s service and the service of humanity”
To foster civic engagement among America’s future, our conference draws approximately 700 participants from all across the political spectrum and from all over the country. Under the direction of Princeton undergraduates, high school students simulate the experience of serving in all three branches of the American government by debating bills in Congress, sitting on the bench as a Supreme Court Justice, and counseling our Commander-in-Chief as a member of the Presidential Cabinet.

mpu:53087.description: To cultivate a South Asian community and express ourselves through the form of dance.

mpu:53088.description:
The Nassau Literary Review is the second oldest undergraduate literary magazine in the nation and the oldest student publication at Princeton University.
Since 1842, NassLit has been an integral part of the Princeton artistic tradition, providing a forum for student writers, poets, and artists. It was in our pages that many of Princeton’s most celebrated alumni – including F. Scott Fitzgerald, Galway Kinnell, and Jonathan Safran Foer, among others – first published their work, and we continue to seek out the best literary and artistic talents on campus today.

mpu:53089.tagline: Come right in, sit right down, and make yourself at home!
mpu:53089.description: The Princeton Nassoons is one of the world's finest collegiate performance ensembles. Founded in 1941, we are a low-voice, TTBB a cappella group that has sung our signature four-, five-, and six-part harmonies alongside the likes of Ella Fitzgerald, the Lettermen, and Ben Folds. We connect Princeton's past and present through our arrangements, campus engagement, and sense of family.
mpu:53089.whatWeDo: As a member you can look forward to finding a family in the Nassoons. In the past, we have toured the globe three times a year, sharing our music, dancing, and jokes with audiences that have included three U.S. presidents, royalty, vacationers in Cancun, screaming school children in Hong Kong, and socialites in Monte Carlo. All of these trips are fully funded by the group at no cost to you! You'll also have the opportunity to arrange songs of your choice and sing with some of your best friends.
mpu:53089.goals: We aim to create a welcoming environment to sing, travel, and share our love of music! While we do not currently plan to hold auditions this spring, we would still love to get to know you and we hope you'll join us in the fall!

mpu:53090.description: To increase the number of culturally responsible Black engineers who excel academically, succeed professionally, and positively impact the community

mpu:53091.description:
Natives at Princeton (NAP) is a student organization that provides a support network for and empowers American Indian, Alaska Native, Native Hawaiian, and other Indigenous students. NAP works to increase the visibility of Native peoples and ideas, as well as to foster greater awareness and understanding of Native issues. Each year NAP invites Native speakers to campus, holds events, hosts Native American Heritage Month in collaboration with the Carl A. Fields Center for Equality and Cultural Understanding. Each semester, members of NAP represent Princeton at the Ivy Native Conference.
NAP works closely with the Princeton Indigenous Advocacy Coalition, the Princeton American Indian and Indigenous Studies Working Group, Nuclear Princeton, and the Native American and Indigenous Studies Initiative. Natives at Princeton is a Sustainability Student Group Partner through Princeton’s office of Sustainability.

mpu:53092.description: Our mission is to celebrate and promote the rich cultural heritage of Nepal, fostering a sense of belonging and unity among Nepali students and allies at Princeton. We strive to create a supportive environment where members can connect, share experiences, and engage in meaningful dialogue about our cultural identity and traditions. Through cultural events, educational programs, and community service, we aim to raise awareness of Nepal’s diverse culture, advocate for the needs of our community, and contribute to the broader university's multicultural environment. We are committed to promoting inclusivity, diversity, and mutual respect both within our group and across the campus community

mpu:53094.description:
The mission of Princeton Neuroscience Network is to connect undergraduate students interested in neuroscience and medicine and facilitate outreach events to engage students in the greater Princeton area.
This organization is open to all Princeton University students interested in supporting our organization’s mission, regardless of identity, such as race, sex, ethnicity, national origin, or other protected characteristics.

mpu:53096.tagline: Princeton's premier low-voice R&B and Soul a cappella group since 2006
mpu:53096.description: Bringing R&B and soul to Princeton since 2006.

mpu:53097.description: The Princeton Open Campus Coalition exists to foster a campus environment free of intolerance and fear by promoting academic freedom and encouraging free inquiry, civil dialogue, and robust discussion of all matters.
mpu:53097.whatWeDo: You will get to challenge your opinions with others who hold different opinions and come from different backgrounds but are dedicated to free speech. You will also be able to engage with scholars, lawyers, and faculty who specialize in this area.
mpu:53097.goals:
The aim of POCC is to promote academic freedom and free speech and protect the free speech rights of Princeton affiliates.
The organization aims to promote free speech themed events from various organizations on campus or on our on volition and to create an environment with civil discourse through our podcast, where we invite experts on first amendment rights and issues as well as faculty, students and guests to discuss various subjects or express different opinions that are normally not brought up in current discourse.
The organization aims to maintain communication with the administration and other constituents of the university to make sure that the ideas and free speech rights of all students and faculty are protected.
Finally we aim to share multiple perspectives, and request more, to curate on our website pocc.princeton.edu

mpu:53098.tagline: Prince­ton Opera Com­pany is the university’s student-run opera orga­ni­za­tion. A rec­og­nized stu­dent orga­ni­za­tion under the Prince­ton Under­grad­u­ate Stu­dent Gov­ern­ment and Prince­ton Arts Coun­cil, we are cel­e­brat­ing the com­ple­tion of its second year as an addi­tion to the Prince­ton arts com­mu­nity. The com­pany shares this won­der­ful art form with the Prince­ton com­mu­nity through reper­toire con­certs, mas­ter classes, opera scenes perfor­mances, excur­sions to New York opera per­for­mances, new music col­lab­o­ra­tions, and fully staged opera pro­duc­tions.
mpu:53098.description: The mission of the Company is to promote operatic performance and education within the Princeton community through activities including, but not limited to, full opera productions, scenes concerts, instructional rehearsals, masterclasses, competitions, opera history workshops, and social events open to members of the Company, Princeton University, and the general public.
mpu:53098.goals: We aim to fill the operatic void on campus by giving students opportunities to perform, produce, compose, direct, learn, and love opera on campus and to provide a visible community for students passionate about this art form. We seek to keep opera on campus.

mpu:53099.description: Forward-thinking chamber music society based in Princeton University
mpu:53099.whatWeDo: Collaborate, perform, and tour with experienced and dedicated classical musicians (piano, strings, winds, brass, classical guitar) at Princeton University

mpu:53100.description:
We are a club consisting mainly of undergraduate and graduate students, but we also organize events open to the entire community. The purpose of our organization is to celebrate Hellenic culture while aiming to develop a better understanding of current issues in Greece and Cyprus.
This organization is open to all Princeton University students interested in supporting our organization’s mission, regardless of
identity, such as race, sex, ethnicity, national origin, or other protected characteristics.
mpu:53100.whatWeDo:
A Hellenic cultural club has existed in the past at Princeton University, and its most recent iteration was established in October 2011. Since then, the Orange Pan-Hellenic Association has been regularly active on campus.
- On a regular year, OPA organizes Modern Greek language tables at Mathey and Rocky Colleges, where students and faculty have the opportunity to practice conversational Greek over a meal in the dining hall.
- The club also plans on-campus cultural events and workshops sponsored by the Carl A. Fields Center, USG Projects Board, the Stanley Seeger Center for Hellenic Studies, and numerous academic departments.

mpu:53102.description: PSA strives to create a welcoming space on campus for all Pakistani students and those who would love to learn more about the cultures and traditions of Pakistan.

mpu:53105.tagline: Pioneering the art of collaborative piano.
mpu:53105.description:
As pioneers in the art of collaborative piano, we challenge the notion that piano is only a solo instrument and push the traditional boundaries of how the instrument is performed. Four hands on one piano, ten hands on five pianos, and everything in between - we’ve done it or we’ll do it. Our mission is nothing less than to make beautiful music accessible to all and to spread it around Princeton and the world.
This organization is open to all Princeton University students interested in supporting our organization’s mission, regardless of identity, such as race, sex, ethnicity, national origin, or other protected characteristics.

mpu:53108.tagline: Princeton University Players is an entirely student-run production company that engages theater-lovers and supports theater-makers on Princeton├óÔé¼Ôäós campus and beyond! We provide the opportunity for a wide range of Princeton University students to develop their talents and passions by producing works of established and original musical theater.
mpu:53108.description:
Princeton University Players is an entirely student-run production company that engages theater-lovers and supports theater-makers on Princeton’s campus and beyond. We provide the opportunity for a wide range of Princeton University students to develop their talents and passions by producing works of established and original musical theater.
We believe that the highest quality product emerges from an enjoyable and enriching process within an open and welcoming community. We aim to foster a safe, creative environment by constantly striving to uplift the voices of artists of all identities and giving the well-being and personal safety of our artists the utmost priority.
PUP is committed to combatting discrimination on the basis of race, religion, gender, gender identity and/or expression, ability, nationality, socioeconomic class, and sexual orientation, in all of its practices and operations, including but not limited to: casting, audition processes, proposals processes, rehearsals, productions, board elections, and social gatherings.
At PUP, we work to consistently uphold our core values: creative expression, equity, inclusivity, accessibility, and friendship. We believe in valuing our artists as human beings first and performers second. We value cultivating joyful creative processes, uplifting artists of all experience levels, and fostering an encouraging community. We are students empowering other students in their artistic endeavors.

mpu:53109.description:
The Princeton Poker Club provides undergraduate and graduate students with opportunities to play,
study, and improve at poker through regular games, workshops, and competitive tournaments.
This organization is open to all Princeton University students interested in supporting our organization’s mission, regardless of identity, such as race, sex, ethnicity, national origin, or other protected characteristics.

mpu:53110.description: The Princeton Polish Society seeks to foster a Polish community on campus and give students space to interact with the diversity of Polish culture, history, society, cuisine, and language. While many of the society's members are of Polish origin, we are equally welcoming to all enthusiasts of Poland and those curious to discover its cultural and academic richness. This organization is open to all Princeton University students interested in supporting our organization’s mission, regardless of identity, such as race, sex, ethnicity, national origin, or other protected characteristics.

mpu:53111.description: The Princeton Pre-Law Society is an undergraduate pre-professional student organization dedicated to equipping students with comprehensive knowledge and resources about law school and legal professions. Our mission is to foster a supportive community where aspiring legal professionals can explore their interests, gain valuable insights, and prepare for successful careers in the field of law. Through educational events, mentorship programs, networking opportunities, and guidance on the law school application process, we aim to empower our members to achieve their academic and professional goals while upholding the values of integrity, excellence, and social responsibility.

mpu:53113.description: To represent the interests of the lesbian, gay, bisexual, transgender, queer, intersex, asexual and questioning, and other members of the community at Princeton University. This includes acting as resources of information and encouraging dialogue about LGBTQIA+ experiences. To provide an accepting and affirming social environment for all lesbian, gay, bisexual, transgender, queer, intersex, asexual, questioning, and others members of the community at Princeton University, regardless of whether they are out of the closet. To work towards deliberately inclusive programming and co-sponsorship with other Princeton student groups to center intersectionality, including (but not limited to) race, religion, ethnicity, nationality, disability, class, etc.

mpu:53116.description:
The Princeton Astronomy Club is dedicated to: increasing access to astronomy both as a hobby and a field; enabling and facilitating inclusion in astronomy; creating a community of individuals interested in Astronomy that spans all undergraduate classes; increasing connection between astronomical researchers and undergraduate students; and encouraging communication and interaction between students of different classes, as well as with astronomy-related faculty.
This organization is open to all Princeton University students interested in supporting our organization’s mission, regardless of identity, such as race, sex, ethnicity, national origin, or other protected characteristics.

mpu:53120.description:
The Princeton Birding Society was founded in 2019, and is dedicated to promoting and encouraging:
• Love and appreciation for our feathered friends in an inclusive, supportive group environment
• An awareness of natural spaces and the importance of avian biodiversity, both on the Princeton campus and within a variety of local ecosystems through organized excursions
• Participation in meaningful conservation initiatives and events designed to foster a closer relationship among students, community members, and birds
• Contributions to valuable citizen science projects through the study of local bird populations

mpu:53121.description:
Princeton Black Men's Association was created in 2019 after new leadership took over to rebrand the former Black men's organization on campus. PBMA is committed fostering an inclusive and engaged community for Black men on Princeton's campus.
The core values of PBMA are as follows:
Create an unrivaled, engaged environment for Princeton's Black Men
Improve the Black experience on Princeton’s campus for men and women
Empower Black male excellence and holding each other to high standards
To adhere to our core values inclusive PBMA has Community Dialogues, Study Breaks, Career-oriented presentations, Mentorship Pods and more.

mpu:53126.description:
PEESA’s overall mission contains three main goals:
To become an affinity space that can be enjoyed by all members
To be platform for Ethiopians and Eritreans to express the many cultures that make up the Habesha population to the Princeton community
To act as an open resource for those in the Princeton community who wish to learn more about aspects of habesha culture(s)

mpu:53127.description:
Per the national office of the Federalist Society, our purpose and mission can be described (like the national organization and all of its chapters) as the following:
"The Federalist Society for Law and Public Policy Studies is a group of conservatives and libertarians interested in the current state of the legal order. It is founded on the principles that the state exists to preserve freedom, that the separation of governmental powers is central to our Constitution, and that it is emphatically the province and duty of the judiciary to say what the law is, not what it should be. The Society seeks both to promote an awareness of these principles and to further their application through its activities."
Our motto, "Discuss, Debate, Decide" perfectly summarizes our mission on Princeton's campus.

mpu:53128.description:
Celebrating the Filipino community and culture at Princeton.
This organization is open to all Princeton University students interested in supporting our organization’s mission, regardless of identity, such as race, sex, ethnicity, national origin, or other protected characteristics.

mpu:53131.description: HOSA -- Future Health Professionals is an international student organization endorsed by the U.S. Department of Education with over 245,000 members around the world. The mission of HOSA is to empower students to become leaders in the global health community through education, collaboration, and experience. HOSA hosts over 55 competitive events annually at Regional, State, and International Leadership Conferences. These competitions range from Health Science and Health Professions events to Teamwork and Leadership events. With an array of unique competitive events, students with any level of interest in healthcare have the opportunity to showcase their abilities, step out of their comfort zones, master new skills alongside their peers, and explore their passion for healthcare. In addition to competitive events, HOSA offers internships, scholarships, and service recognition at the state and international levels.

mpu:53133.description: PLASA is a university-wide undergraduate student-led organization that provides a space for building community and belonging at Princeton, and encourages education across different Latine backgrounds and multicultural identities.

mpu:53134.description: The goal of the PLJ is to provide Princeton University and the public with an impactful space for law-related discourse through our publication of undergraduate legal scholarship and guest speaker events.

mpu:53136.description:
Princeton Peer Nightline is an anonymous peer listening service. Our listeners are undergraduate students of Princeton University who have been trained and certified as helpline volunteers. We provide empathetic, non-judgmental support to Princeton University students who wish to share a problem, are in need of information, or just want to talk about whatever is on their mind. Whether it's relationships, academic stress, a fight with a friend or a parent, depression, eating disorders, suicidal thoughts, roommate troubles, or you just had a really bad day and want to vent, we're here to listen and make sure that no student has to face their problems alone.
Peer Nightline volunteers do not provide professional counseling, but rather supportive listening. Students in crisis will be directed to appropriate professional resources including the CPS counselor on call. We highly recommend that students who are experiencing mental health emergencies reach out to the on call counselor at CPS (609) 258-3141 or to Public Safety at (609) 258-1000.

mpu:53141.description: Founded in 2015, the Princeton Rocketry Club is a fast-growing organization of about 100 students. We give members the opportunity to gain hands-on experience designing, building, and flying a wide variety of aerospace vehicles. Besides the number of current projects we are working on, we also host events such as prominent speaker talks and on-campus launches for the general University community. We seek to push the limits and educate others about space.

mpu:53142.tagline: Princeton Science of Psychedelics - let's talk.
mpu:53142.description:
The mission of the Princeton Science of Psychedelics Club (PSPC) is to facilitate a healthy environment for discussion and study of topics related to psychedelics - and more broadly, consciousness, on Princeton’s campus and the larger community.
The PSPC will do this by promoting psychedelic research and professional development, as well as by spreading awareness of the science, policies, history and applications of psychedelics.

mpu:53143.description: We play casual soccer and organize campus wide soccer tournaments.

mpu:53144.description: PSPS offers a community dedicated to representing the interests of physics students, fostering a social environment, and providing academic resources to support their success. It is especially important for PSPS to acknowledge and address the ongoing underrepresentation of women, people of color, international students, and LGBTQ+ individuals in STEM, and to create an environment where physics students can excel academically, professionally, and socially.

mpu:53145.description: Princeton Student Veterans supports student veterans throughout their undergraduate experience by fostering professional development, community, and service. We connect members with career opportunities, build a lasting network of veterans within the Princeton community, and extend that support beyond campus through outreach initiatives. Grounded in the shared values of leadership and service that our members bring from their time in uniform, Princeton Student Veterans exists to help student veterans succeed at Princeton and beyond.

mpu:53149.description: PURJ is Princeton’s first and only peer-reviewed academic journal, highlighting top-quality research performed by Princeton undergraduates across all academic pursuits, including the natural sciences, humanities, engineering, social sciences, and arts. We aim to provide a multidisciplinary forum through which Princeton students can share their scholarly findings and engage with the broader research community. Submitted manuscripts will undergo a rigorous peer review process involving both Princeton undergraduates and faculty.
mpu:53149.whatWeDo: Although PURJ is a new student publication, we have already received extensive support from prominent professors, who will work with us throughout the year to ensure the quality of our publications by participating in the peer review process. These faculty members span over 20 different academic departments on campus and include Dean of the Graduate School and Professor of Electrical Engineering Sanjeev Kulkarni, Donald R. Dixon ’69 and Elizabeth W. Dixon Professor of Mechanical and Aerospace Engineering Howard Stone, and Professor of Physics and Astrophysical Sciences Jo Dunkley, among others. We have also received the support of many institutional offices at Princeton, including the Office of the Dean of Research, the Office of Undergraduate Research, the Humanities Council, the Lewis Center for the Arts, and the Office of the Dean of Undergraduate Students.

mpu:53151.tagline: Where Business Acumen Meets Social Impact
mpu:53151.description:
Where Business Acumen Meets Social Impact
Founded in 2009, we are Princeton University’s largest and oldest student-run consulting group, and we’re here to prove that professional development and civic service are not mutually exclusive. Adopting a selective admissions process, we pair top student talent from Princeton with the world’s leading non-profit organizations, businesses, and social enterprises.
PUNC’s student consultants bring with them a broad range of experience that spans across majors, nationalities, interests, and professional working experiences. Our members are passionate about making a measurable difference for our partner organizations.

mpu:53155.description: Princeton Women in Economics and Policy (WEP) is an organization that seeks to inspire and empower women undergraduates who are interested in studying or building careers in economics, business, finance, politics, or public policy. Our mission is to leverage the collective experience to provide mentorship and resources. With this goal in mind, we host career-oriented workshops, speaking events, and a year-long mentorship program connecting members on campus.

mpu:53158.description: Princeton Pro-Life seeks to be a community of pro-life students at Princeton that educates themselves and others on issues relating to abortion, sparks thoughtful and respectful dialogue surrounding abortion on campus, serves and supports local women in unexpected pregnancies, and equips students to be bold, effective, and compassionate ambassadors for the pro-life cause.

mpu:53162.description:
Princeton University Zealously Zany Logical Enigma Solvers
A place for all types of puzzlers, hunt-style and non-hunt style.
Host of Princeton Puzzle Hunt. Join our discord server: https://discord.gg/ZtXvbeTxWR

mpu:53163.description: Providing a warm, welcoming space to Questbridge Scholars attending Princeton!

mpu:53164.description:
Quipfire! aims to create improv comedy with a foundation of fun, support, professionalism, passion and love in the way we treat each other as a family and in the scenes we perform together on and offstage.
As members and improvisers together, we understand that in order to practice risk and rigor in our work, we must back it up with safety and accountability.
This means that trusting one another and feeling safe, comfortable, and secure go hand in hand with creating quality improv together.
As members of Quipfire!, we commit ourselves to having fun and working hard on and offstage. We recognize that the risks we take in our improv should always be supported by our fellow members. We will always have each other’s backs and not allow circumstances to reach a point that denies the pure enjoyment of Quipfire! improv comedy. When these values are reflected among us, our work is at its best.
This is a living, breathing document, and can be amended at any point to reflect the values of the group.

mpu:53166.description:
Princeton Racing Electric (PRE) is a student-run organization dedicated to developing sustainably powered, high-performance electric vehicles. Founded in 2013, our team designs and builds all-electric race cars to participate in the annual international Formula Hybrid + Electric competition. PRE has taken the second-place prize in 2017, 2018, and 2019, in addition to winning the IEEE Excellence in EV Engineering Award in 2018 and 2019 as well as the IEEE Excellence in Project Management Award in 2019, showcasing our commitment to interdisciplinary teamwork and engineering excellence.
We also strive to provide a hands-on, practical engineering experience to Princeton undergraduates by engaging our team members in the project-based learning environment of a multi-year electric vehicle build. By providing for direct student involvement in projects employing scientific principles in fields including carbon-fiber composites, structural analysis, high-voltage design, and electronic signal processing, we hope to prepare a new generation of innovators in alternative energy technology. By encouraging student leadership and providing practical experience in these critical fields, PRE hopes to foster the next generation of innovators on the path to a sustainable future.
Princeton Racing Electric is open to all Princeton University students interested in supporting our organization’s mission, regardless of identity, such as race, sex, ethnicity, national origin, or other protected characteristics.

mpu:53168.description:
Raqs: Princeton Belly Dance Company was founded in 2000, after receiving inspiration from the belly dance classes taught at Dillon Gym by Kim Leary. Wanting to bring the rich history and beauty of belly dance to the Princeton community, the students in the class decided to form a troupe. As an established performance group on campus, we are a welcoming and tight-knit community of dancers from all over the world. Our troupe embraces many levels of experience, from pre-professionals to complete beginners, with the ultimate goal of body love and empowerment.
This organization is open to all Princeton University students interested in supporting our organization’s mission, regardless of identity, such as race, sex, ethnicity, national origin, or other protected characteristics.

mpu:53169.description: The Princeton Undergraduate Real Estate Group aims to promote the real estate industry to current undergraduate students through its partnership with the Princeton Alumni Real Estate Network. We host networking events with various alumni working in real estate, send out newsletters, and provide student and alumni career mentorship to those seeking a career in real estate. Email pureg@princeton.edu for more information or to join the club; all levels of real estate knowledge and interest are welcome.
mpu:53169.goals: Our goal for 2021-22 is to attend the Cornell International Real Estate Case Competition for the first time!

mpu:53171.description: Rise Up Singing is a pick-up sing-along group. We meet together to play and sing our favorite folk and more songs every Wednesday from 9-11pm! Come find us jamming down in Murray Dodge Café! Rise Up is open to all Princeton University students interested in folk music, regardless of identity, such as race, sex, ethnicity, national origin, or other protected characteristics.
mpu:53171.whatWeDo: There are no membership commitments, just show up when you could use some music! There is no skill requirement and you do not have to play a folk/string instrument to join in!
mpu:53171.goals: To spread love, destress, and share fun music together!

mpu:53172.description:
Roaring 20 is Princeton University's premier co-ed a cappella group, dedicated to performing a dynamic repertoire with a uniquely resonant sound from "Gershwin to Gaga" since 1983. Our past venues range from Princeton University arches to the US Embassy in London and cities such as Paris, Madrid, and Honolulu. Join our family to sing and tour around the world!
For more, visit us at www.princetonroaring20.com and follow us on Instagram (@princetonroaring20)!
[ Website ] www.princetonroaring20.com
[ Spotify ] https://open.spotify.com/artist/0eAFUaTc0hS9enWM6pjyVW
[ Apple Music ] https://music.apple.com/us/artist/princeton-roaring-20/988689597
[ YouTube ] www.youtube.com/@PrincetonRoaring20
[ Instagram ] https://www.instagram.com/princetonroaring20/
mpu:53172.whatWeDo:
- Fully funded (aka, free!) semesterly tours during spring & fall breaks (domestic & international)
- Regularly scheduled events/gigs/performances throughout each semester
- No limit to the genre of music
- Wide range of repertoire
- Entirely student-run
- Inviting, vibrant, and loving community
- Annual song recordings & album releases

mpu:53173.description:
We are Princeton University’s Official Undergraduate Robotics Club. As an official ODUS student group, we welcome undergrads from every year and every major. We strive to provide an environment for Princeton undergrads to collaborate with others who are interested in robotics, no prior experience required!
This organization is open to all Princeton University students interested in supporting our organization’s mission, regardless of identity, such as race, sex, ethnicity, national origin, or other protected characteristics.
mpu:53173.whatWeDo: As a member, you will be able to join any of our project teams for 2024-25: Droid, WALL-E, PacBot, Drone, RoboCup, Bionics, Exoskeleton, Tinker, or Golf Cart, all of which you can learn more about on our website (https://robotics.princeton.edu/). We also provide weekly trainings to learn valuable robotics skills, and fun events throughout the year to meet other students that are passionate about robotics!
mpu:53173.goals: We build robots. Our goal is to give Princeton students a space to learn about robotics whether they come in with no experience at all or have been building robots for years. Through workshops, competitions, and advising, we hope to help anyone and everyone get closer to being to be able to build their dream robot.

mpu:53174.description: The Princeton University Rock Ensemble (PURE) is Princeton’s original student-led rock band, serving riffs, rhythm, and just a touch of sparkle. Our 30+ members span a wide range of instruments beyond what conventionally compose "rock" bands, and our taste in music stretches even further; 100% run by students, PURE is, at its core, an inclusive collection of people bonded by the simple love of music and performance.

mpu:53176.description: Our mission is to create a space for the greater Princeton-based Russian-speaking Community and promote Russian Language and Culture for the wider audience. Additionally, we regularly host educational events about Russian history and culture. We are also known as "Rusyak". =)

mpu:53178.description:
