Scholars of Finance is the first nonprofit organization dedicated to developing undergraduate finance students into the next generation of highly capable financial executives who will act and lead with integrity and a commitment to serving the greater good.
This organization is open to all Princeton University students interested in supporting our organization’s mission, regardless of identity, such as race, sex, ethnicity, national origin, or other protected characteristics.

mpu:53179.description:
Come join Princeton Science Olympiad!! We are a non-profit student organization dedicated to inspiring creative problem solving, STEM literacy, and love for learning through our annual invitational tournament. In normal years, we spend fall and winter preparing to host a tournament in February for high schoolers from all around the country, focusing on 23 different scientific fields ranging from epidemiology to cryptography to forensics to electrical engineering to oceanography and everywhere in between.
We will also engage in outreach and mentoring, hoping to make advanced science education more accessible. We were the first college invitational to waive registration fees, and we offer a financial aid program to schools in need hoping to attend, so we’re very excited to hear your ideas about how to make STEM more equitable.
Apply to join our executive board to plan the tournament and work on graphic design, test review, communications, webmastering, and more! Or apply to be an event supervisor or a member of the outreach team to write tests and teach high schoolers. We'll also be taking volunteers for the day of the tournament to help run the events and answer questions - let us know if you're interested!
We can be found at scioly.princeton.edu and instagram/princetonscioly. You can also contact us through this page, at scioly@princeton.edu, or by reaching out to one of our tournament directors at ec1261@princeton.edu, malachi.noel@princeton.edu, or lopen@princeton.edu

mpu:53183.description: To create a caring, inclusive, and fun environment in which to grow and share through music.

mpu:53184.description: The Simulation Games Union is the central hub for recreational board games and other non-computer simulation games, including tabletop roleplaying games. SGU strives to make gaming accessible to all, as well as create a community on and off campus where everyone can share a love of these games. SGU is also responsible for the implementation of PrinceCon, the oldest extant volunteer-run fantasy roleplaying convention in the nation.

mpu:53185.description:
Six14 is a Christian dance company dedicated to glorifying God and sharing the gospel through various forms of dance, including hip hop, lyrical, contemporary, or praise dance.
----------------------------------------------
Six14 is a community of believers who seek to glorify God by first and foremost strengthening their relationship with God and pouring into the lives of each other.
- One thing I ask from the Lord, this only do I seek: that I may dwell in the house of the Lord all the days of my life, to gaze on the beauty of the Lord and to seek him in his temple. Psalm 27:4
- Draw near to God, and he will draw near to you James 4:8
- A new commandment I give to you, that you love one another: just as I have loved you, you also are to love one another. By this all people will know that you are my disciples, if you have love for one another John 13:34-35
Six14 is a company of dancers who believe that dance and movement is an expression of worship, and in doing so, offer their devotion, time, and abilities as dancers up to Christ.
- You have turned for me my mourning into dancing; you have loosed my sackcloth and clothed me with gladness Psalm 30:11

mpu:53187.description:
- provide a community for students born and raised on the African continent as well as share and celebrate the diversity of their origins with each other;
- increase awareness of the diversity of African countries and their different cultures within the Princeton community
support such identifying incoming Princeton students in adjusting to the academic and social life at Princeton university
- offer students hailing from these countries a safe platform to share their thoughts and experiences as well as practice their cultures with people from similar backgrounds
- have an organized platform through which to contribute to Princeton’s cultural affinity groups
- create a mentorship program for undergraduate students by African graduate students in relation to the pursuing of their future goals

mpu:53188.description: The Princeton Society of Hispanic Professional Engineers (SHPE) Chapter is dedicated to empowering Hispanic students in the fields of science, technology, engineering, and mathematics (STEM). Our mission is to build the professional skills of our members, equipping them for success in their future careers. We strive to create safe, inclusive spaces where students can grow academically, socially, and personally, fostering a supportive community that celebrates our diverse backgrounds and shared ambitions. Through mentorship, networking, and collaborative opportunities, we aim to inspire and uplift the next generation of Hispanic leaders in STEM.

mpu:53189.description:
Princeton Society of Women Engineers is an organization dedicated to promoting a strong sense of community among female BSE students.
Princeton SWE is dedicated to:
1) promoting a sense of community among female B.S.E. students, professors, and alumnae of Princeton
2) introducing younger girls to the various opportunities offered by studying engineering.
mpu:53189.whatWeDo: As a member you will connect and meet other women engineers within the undergraduate class, but also the grad school and alumni. We hold study breaks and other social events throughout the year for interested students. Our calendar also includes various industry outreach opportunities as well as community volunteering in Princeton's high school and girl scout troops.
mpu:53189.goals: Traditionally, engineering has been thought of as being predominantly male. Although this trend is reversing, in general, engineering has much greater salary parity between men and women than most other fields. Engineers are at the forefront of the development of the technology that drives our society forward. It is our aim to continue to promote these fields to women who might not have considered studying them, and to offer support to the women who do.

mpu:53193.description: Devoted to building and maintaining a sense of belonging and inclusivity among South Asian communities at Princeton, the Princeton South Asian Student Association (SASA) organizes study breaks, workshops, lectures, and celebrations for the the South Asian community and its friends at Princeton.

mpu:53194.description: The nation's first south asian theatre group.

mpu:53205.description: Princeton Students for Reproductive Justice (PSRJ) exists to educate the University community about reproductive health and rights, to translate increased awareness into pro-choice activism on campus, and to serve as a coalition partner to state, national, and international reproductive rights efforts.

mpu:53208.description: Swara is Princeton's Indian music club, specializing in both classical Indian music as well as a capella! We aim to promote Indian music in a variety of ways; student performances (including virtual performances), workshops for students interested in learning about Indian music, concerts by the world's leading artists (free for students), and guest lectures. Within the group, we also make music together and present to each other on various aspects of the music on a weekly basis. We would love to have anyone who's interested; you don't have to perform or even know anything about the music to get involved.
mpu:53208.whatWeDo: Attending weekly practices and presentations, interacting with professional guest musicians
mpu:53208.goals:
- Learn about and explore Indian music together as a group through discussion, practice, and performance
- Share Indian classical music with the campus community by hosting concerts and conversations with professional artists
- Build a performing group for South Asian a capella to perform at our annual showcase and gigs across campus

mpu:53209.description: Sympoh is Princeton University's only B-boy/B-girl crew. We specialize in elemental hip hop dance: breaking, popping, and locking. We've become prominent among the hip hop community of this region through participating in and hosting underground B-boy battles, as well as hip hop education. We organize community outreach projects through hip hop culture across the mid-Atlantic region. We are also intricately involved with Princeton's performing arts community, choreographing and freestyling multiple performances each month, and creating a full-scale production that sells out every spring.
mpu:53209.whatWeDo: Membership is open to dancers of all experience levels and styles. Anyone who joins will become part of a community of dancers striving to collaborate, create, and improve.
mpu:53209.goals: Sympoh aims to educate the Princeton community on the foundational elements of hip-hop: graffiti, MC'ing, DJ'ing, and the dance: popping, locking, and breaking; with a primary focus on the latter. Sympoh has maintained a steady involvement with Princeton's Annual Hip Hop Symposium-performing frequently each year. Sympoh hosts B-Boy "Jams" each year, and invites the campus community.

mpu:53210.tagline: This organization is open to all Princeton University students interested in supporting our organization’s mission, regardless of identity, such as race, sex, ethnicity, national origin, or other protected characteristics.
mpu:53210.description: The Taiwanese American Students Association is a cultural group dedicated to promoting an understanding of and appreciation for Taiwanese culture and heritage on the Princeton campus.

mpu:53211.description:
Facilitate experiential education and cultivate relationships to create a strong, lasting connection to Israel for emerging professionals.
Through real-world education, consulting, and financial projects, TAMID at Princeton will provide a hands-on opportunity to develop practical skills, gain industry experience, and enhance professional growth.

mpu:53212.description:
Dear Undergrads, Grad Students, Faculty, and Staff, welcome to the Princeton Tango Club!
Join us and share the joy of Argentine Tango with the Princeton community. Learn tango in our
- Beginner classes (Mondays @ 7pm)
- Intermediate classes (Mondays @ 8:30pm)
- Guided Practicas (Sundays @ 2pm)
- Events and social dancing activities
Classes schedules might vary depending on room availability, but they are always on Mondays evening!Check our calendar at https://www.princetontangoclub.com/event-calendar/
Our classes are beginner-friendly throughout the year, so do not fear to join us any time. No partner, experience, or material necessary to attend, although you will appreciate wearing flexible and slippery shoes. Nevertheless, ask us for dancing socks at the beginning of the class if you feel like your shoes are not "slippery enough". Classes are led by our incredible instructors Sean Ericson, Jacqueline Pham, Amelia Foss, and Miloš Nikolić.
See you on Monday!

mpu:53213.description:
TapCats is Princeton's first, only, and best tap dance group! Whether you've been tapping all your life or never put on a tap shoe before, we welcome you to join the TapCats family, and you’ll be placed at a level that best suits your experience! Join us for our big yearly show as well as our (newly introduced) halloween and spring arch-taps! Whether you want to create beautiful rhythm on stage or support the creative offstage side, TapCats is a truly inclusive and fun environment where we get to share and spread our love for tap dance.
Instagram: @princetontapcats

mpu:53217.description: Thaigers' mission is to create an inclusive space for Thai students, both undergraduate and graduate, as well as the broader campus community, to come together to share, celebrate, and promote Thai culture and traditions.

mpu:53219.description:
The Daily Princetonian is the daily independent student newspaper of Princeton University. Our paper is student-run, not-for-profit, and financially independent from the University. We’re one of the oldest college newspapers in the country, covering Princeton since 1876. But we’re also looking forward – with blossoming multimedia journalism sections, digital design and virtual engagement opportunities, and much more.
The ‘Prince’ is dedicated to serving Princetonians past, present, and future through transparent, accurate, and empathetic reporting. We seek to inform and engage our readers by delivering reliable, timely, and truthful news and commentary that matter. We aim to drive campus conversation, uphold high journalistic standards, and innovate in how we tell stories.
mpu:53219.whatWeDo: Members will have the unparalleled opportunity to work at a respected news organization in a range of capacities while engaging with a welcoming community of students.
mpu:53219.goals:
We are dedicated to transparency. The ‘Prince’ wishes to show itself and the members of the Orange Bubble as they are. This extends beyond our reporting. The ‘Prince’ makes it its mission to not only offer a window into Princeton life, but also to share the perspectives of those involved in that collective life, so that they can share their stories and make themselves known.
We are dedicated to diversity. The ‘Prince’ strives to have a staff that is representative of the student body in order to be most attentive to all aspects of campus life and ensure the inclusion of those voices that have been traditionally excluded from both the larger journalism industry and the ‘Prince’ itself. Princeton’s story is not and will never be complete until all its voices are heard.
We are dedicated to intentionality. As a paper financially independent from the University, we have the opportunity to shine a light on all aspects of Princeton, whether in critique or in praise of Old Nassau. We seek to be intentional about the platform we provide and to whom we provide it, ensuring that all those who read, view, or listen to our content come away from the ‘Prince’ more informed and better connected.
We are dedicated to community. We are unique among professional publications in that our members are embedded in the community they serve. Moreover, the digital age requires a new understanding of journalism that extends beyond the print medium. It requires a multiplicity of skills as well as voices, and we seek to weave together the talents of Princeton’s best writers, reporters, editors, designers, photographers, videographers, artists, cartoonists, and entrepreneurs to bring Princeton’s paper of record forward into the future.

mpu:53221.description: Creating a space for Italians to connect and speak Italian together; enabling anyone who wants to experience and learn more about Italian culture.

mpu:53226.description: As the only student theatre on Princeton University’s campus with a permanent space that is completely administered by students, Theatre Intime is committed to producing high quality work for the Princeton student community as well as the greater Princeton area. Intime has the unique opportunity to serve as a laboratory for students’ continued development as theatre makers, promote collaboration throughout the production process, and operate as a student-driven host for the arts community on campus.

mpu:53227.description: The NROTC program was established to develop midshipmen mentally, morally, and physically to imbue them with the highest ideals of duty, and loyalty, and with the core values of honor, courage, and commitment in order to commission as naval officers who possess a basic professional background, are motivated toward careers in the naval service, and have a potential for future development in mind and character so as to assume the highest responsibilities of command, citizenship, and government.
mpu:53227.whatWeDo: The NROTC Scholarship pays the students' tuition, uniforms, and lab related fees. A textbook stipend is also provided to assist with books. It also provides the student a stipend every month during the school year, this increases as you complete years in the program, to help with the cost of living.
mpu:53227.goals: To prepare MIDN mentally, morally, and physically to commission as naval and marine corps officers upon graduation.

mpu:53228.description:
Tiger Investments is Princeton’s oldest student-run investing club, focusing on financial education and investment research. Our mission is to help members gain the foundational tools they need to navigate the investing world and to offer various opportunities to apply these skills.
Because education is one of our major focuses, many of our early meetings are focused on teaching our members the basics of fundamental analysis and financial modeling. Other core activities include investment research, analytical discussions, internal stock pitch presentations, and virtual portfolio management competitions. We also host educational networking events with several firms throughout the year.
mpu:53228.whatWeDo:
The officer team has been working hard to continually improve every member’s experience. A few of the new opportunities and resources that we are putting together for Tiger Investments this year include:
- A Tiger Investments alumni directory
- Virtual bonding and social events
- Mentorship opportunities with upperclassmen
- Resume workshops and mock interviews
We will also be bringing speakers with experiences from different areas of finance (investment banking, venture capital, private equity, etc). The global pandemic has significantly impacted everyone’s lives, but we will try to make sure that students can still enjoy opportunities and events organized by Tiger Investments.

mpu:53229.description:
Founded in 1882, The Princeton Tiger is the nation’s third oldest college humor magazine, 144 years young (though we don’t look a day over 90). We’re funny, we’re marginally literate, and we’re free, distributed to every undergraduate room, common area, dining hall, eating club, and elite social circle in Princeton, even the equestrian team (when they get off their high horses).
This organization is open to all Princeton University students interested in supporting our organization’s mission, regardless of identity, such as race, sex, ethnicity, national origin, or other protected characteristics.

mpu:53237.description: Triangle is a student performing arts group that performs original, student-written musical comedy. We perform a show in the McCarter Theatre every fall, in addition to an annual national tour and Reunions encore, along with our spring show and frosh week show.
mpu:53237.whatWeDo: Triangle's members are spread between five "sides" cast, tech, business, writers, and the pit orchestra, so there are lots of ways to get involved and learn new skills in an amazing community of people!

mpu:53238.description: Triple 8 is Princeton's premier East Asian dance company. Our mission is to use dance as an artistic means of exposing East Asian culture to the Princeton community. Known for our diversity of styles, we choreograph and perform traditional Asian dances, contemporary, hip hop, and martial arts. We are a company full of dancers with diverse backgrounds and experience levels, some of whom had no previous dance experience and many of whom are members of other dance groups. But above all, Triple 8 is a close-knit family - we eat together, study together, cry together, laugh together. And through it all, we make some of our fondest memories together on campus.

mpu:53239.description: Introducing Turkish culture and language at Princeton University.

mpu:53241.description: We seek to foster a welcoming, inclusive community for students interested in and currently pursuing physics and related fields! This organization is open to all Princeton University students interested in supporting our organization’s mission, regardless of identity, such as race, sex, ethnicity, national origin, or other protected characteristics.

mpu:53242.description: We work to represent, serve, and support the undergraduate student body, both individually and collectively, by collaborating with students, administrators, faculty, and other community stakeholders to address student concerns. We encourage all undergraduates to voice their ideas and concerns to USG members while making ourselves accessible, transparent, and accountable. We collaborate with Princeton administrators to revise and propose policies that improve student life, provide high-quality services to students, and organize innovative events to foster a sense of community. We ultimately strive to represent the student body, both individually and collectively, serve them throughout their Princeton experience, and support them thrive through adversity, with advocacy, policy, and programming.
mpu:53242.goals: We ensure that all Princetonians are valued and supported by cultivating a dynamic community in which students can comfortably express and celebrate their diverse backgrounds, talents, and interests. We envision a campus where students are not only empowered but eager to serve their communities.

mpu:53243.description: Welcome to the Princeton United World Colleges Club! We seek to foster a sense of community at Princeton among alumni of the United World College movement, through a variety of different activities.
mpu:53243.goals:
To have weekly study breaks and enjoy brunch together. The purpose is to foster a strong sense of community among UWC students and faculty.
UWC Buddy Program
We plan on continuing a version of the UWC Buddy program, which has been an enormous success in the past. The program consists of buddy pairs getting a meal around campus, in order to help freshmen with any issues they may have, and to hopefully provide some guidance during their first semester in Princeton.

mpu:53244.description: The University Press Club is a group of freelance journalists based on Princeton's campus that cover local and national stories for outside publications.

mpu:53245.description: Founded in Spring 2015, the Princeton US-China Coalition (PUCC) seeks to create a transnational coalition of student leaders poised to face the issues at the forefront of US-China policy. Our vision is to serve as one of many intellectual and cultural links between the United States and China, creating a broad, worldwide coalition of student leaders to foster meaningful dialogue between the two countries.

mpu:53247.description: To bring Vietnamese culture to the students of Princeton.

mpu:53248.description:
Founded in 2011, VTone is Princeton's first and only East Asian music group. "V" stands for the Roman numeral 5 and alludes to the pentatonic scale of traditional East Asian music. With our music, we aim to intrigue, inspire, and invigorate a worldly fusion of the arts.
Every year, we explore genres ranging from ballads and J-rock to rap and K-pop. In the fall semester, VTone joins in Princeton a cappella tradition and holds an annual Fall Arch Sing to perform original a cappella arrangements, covers, and mash-ups composed by members. In our annual spring show, however, we don't limit ourselves to a cappella; that's what makes VTone unique!

mpu:53249.description: The nation's oldest collegiate political, literary, and debate society.

mpu:53250.description: The Wildcats are Princeton's boldest treble voice a cappella group. As we are founded on the motto, "Strong Cats, Strong Voices,” empowerment is a fundamental element of the Wildcats mission. This organization is open to all Princeton University students interested in supporting our organization’s mission, regardless of identity, such as race, sex, ethnicity, national origin, or other protected characteristics.

mpu:53253.description: PWiCS is dedicated to supporting women in computer science through a combination of on-campus mentorship, corporate partnerships, and community outreach.
mpu:53253.whatWeDo: We plan regular mentorship events with opportunities for our members to connect with one another, including study breaks, Big-Little programs, and advising from upperclassmen to underclassmen. We also partner with companies such as Google, Facebook, and Microsoft for information sessions, workshops, talks, and other corporate sponsorship events. Finally, we play an active role in service in our community and beyond, attending the Society of Women Engineers’ annual High School Colloquium and planning computer science workshops for middle school and high school students.

mpu:53255.description: WPRB is a community-supported, non-profit 501(c)3, commercially-licensed freeform radio station. While our studios are located on Princeton University’s campus, we are independently financed and student-managed. Our signal covers a range of approximately 15,000 square miles, serving a population of millions throughout central New Jersey, South Philadelphia, eastern Pennsylvania, Wilmington, DE, and parts of the Jersey Shore. Broadcasting at 14,000 watts of stereo power, our signal is among the strongest in college radio. WPRB’s live internet stream carries our programming across the country and around the globe.

mpu:53257.description: Princeton YDSA is an anti-capitalist group organizing for workplace democracy, political education, labor, social, and ecological justice, and more from a profoundly democratic perspective.

mpu:53258.description: The Albanian-Kosovo Association (AKA) is an affinity group for the Albanian and Kosovar students of Princeton, as well as all those interested in Albanian culture! The AKA looks to build community through casual dinners, as well as cultural and social host events.

mpu:53260.description: Alimtas Bioventures is a subteam of the Princeton Entrepreneurship Club focused on life science entrepreneurship. Our organization is working directly with the Office of Technology Licensing to spin out Princeton University life science discoveries spanning biotechnology, therapeutics, medical technologies, and other subfields from researchers through rigorous due diligence and business planning. We also partner with leading life science venture capital firms and industry companies to deepen our knowledge, methodologies, and networks.

mpu:53261.tagline: Princeton's premier social entrepreneurship non-profit: disrupting education since 2015
mpu:53261.description:
IgniteSTEM is one of the branch organizations of Princeton University’s Entrepreneurship Club. We’re a non-profit dedicated to transforming K-12 education through innovative approaches found in hackathons, design thinking, and maker spaces.
In the past, we have organized conferences and design thinking workshops for STEM educators, as well as compiled innovative STEM resources for educators. This year we wanted to offer something for high school students to introduce them to design thinking and hands-on learning, and have begun hosting Design Challenges for students and educators as well!

mpu:53262.description: New York TigerTrek is an organized trip in which 20 rigorously-selected Princeton undergraduates are offered the opportunity to visit entrepreneurial luminaries at cutting edge start ups, venture capital firms, and corporates in New York City. We hold closed-door only, candid conversations with each leader we meet, granting students insight into the cutting edge of tech.

SVTT gives entrepreneurial Princeton students the opportunity to connect with and learn
from the technology luminaries of Silicon Valley, bringing back an informed perspective
of Bay Area culture to share with peers, drive new student projects, and add meaning to
entrepreneurial activity on campus.

mpu:53266.description:
TigerLaunch is the world’s largest student-run pitch competition, connecting innovators in New York, Singapore, Paris, London, Houston, Princeton, and more. Each year, we bring together 500 of the world’s top student-founders to compete for $60,000 in prizes and mentorship from elite venture capitalists.
The TigerLaunch team organizes numerous startup pitch competitions each year, both in the United States and abroad. We manage every stage of the process from start to finish – including event planning and strategic partnerships, fundraising, branding/marketing, and technical operations.

mpu:53275.description: Founded in 2017, KoKo Pops is Princeton University’s first and only K-pop cover dance company! Driven by a passion for music and movement, our members cover choreography from iconic K-pop groups and K-pop-inspired global artists alike. Our efforts culminate each spring with our annual showcase, where we bring the vibrant energy, precision, and excitement of K-pop choreography to the campus community and beyond!

mpu:53276.description:
The Kurdish Society serves as a portal between Kurdistan and Princeton!
This organization is open to all Princeton University students interested in supporting our organization’s mission, regardless of identity, such as race, sex, ethnicity, national origin, or other protected characteristics.

mpu:53279.description:
The Nassau Weekly is alternative magazine that publishes essays on culture and politics, campus news, op-eds, personal histories, travel journals, reviews of movies and music, humor, poetry and fiction, and achieved things of other modes. It is published weekly during the academic year, and on special schedules during vacations and examination periods, by Nassau Weekly, Inc, a New Jersey not-for-profit corporation.
The Nassau Weekly strives to create an open, inclusive, and diverse community. We welcome and encourage submissions by people of any and all races, ethnicities, gender identities, sexual orientations, abilities, nationalities, religions, and socio-economic statuses.
The Nassau Weekly is distributed free to members of the Princeton University community. Opinions expressed within are those of the writer and not necessarily those of the editorial board.

mpu:53282.description: Princeton's premier student-run chamber orchestra. This organization is open to all Princeton University students interested in supporting our organization’s mission, regardless of identity, such as race, sex, ethnicity, national origin, or other protected characteristics.

mpu:53316.description:
PDAC plans a biannual carnival to bring students with disabilities to campus for a Carnival event with foods, games, and performances. There is a Board of volunteers who establish a timeline for the preparation and execution of the carnival, as well as oversee the tasks being completed. Volunteers can join to become part of the board who plans the event once a year (including logistics, budgeting, training, recruitment) or can volunteer at the event itself, where they are paired with a child with disabilities and spend the carnival hanging out with them and accompanying them throughout the activities.
Frequency/Time Commitment Expected
At the start of the festival, PDAC board members meet once a week for approximately an hour to discuss and plan for the upcoming semester carnival. As the date of the festival approaches, the time commitment for these board meetings increase to at most two and a half hours. Furthermore, once volunteers are recruited, volunteers are required to attend an online training session weeks before the carnival. They are also expected to attend the carnival and pair up with a child with special needs during its entire duration from 1pm to 4pm, in addition to carnival preparation at 12pm and cleanup at the end of the carnival. In total, volunteers participate in the preparation and hosting of the carnival for about 6 hours. This frequency and level of time commitment usually stays the same for both the fall and spring carnival.

Email

PIH collaborates with national governments to provide care and strengthen public health systems in areas including cancer and chronic disease, child health, emergency response, HIV/AIDS, maternal health, and tuberculosis. At Princeton PIH Engage, we will meet with local and national government leaders to share lessons, stories, and positive results from PIH sites and to champion legislation that eliminates barriers to care. Additionally, we will plan and host fundraising events and campaigns to ensure PIH continues to have the resources to prevent preventable deaths and deliver high-quality health care in some of the world’s poorest places. Furthermore, we will host and participate in curricula, webinars, discussions, and events that raise awareness about the systemic inequities that lead to poor health outcomes in impoverished countries, and much more!

Students for Prison Education, Abolition and Reform (SPEAR) is a Princeton University-based student organization that educates, advocates, and agitates against the carceral state on Princeton’s campus, in New Jersey, and beyond. Founded in 2012, SPEAR engages in anti-carceral campus activism, legislative advocacy, community education, and direct engagement with currently and formerly incarcerated peers. SPEAR is committed to centering and uplifting the voices of those directly impacted by the carceral state and all of its intersections with racism, transphobia, classism, homophobia, sexism, ableism, and other systems of oppression and dehumanization. The annual SPEAR conference brings together students, activists, advocates, and academics from across the country for a weekend of lectures, panels, and workshops on Princeton’s campus.

The primary goal of the Muslim Students Association is to serve the needs of the Princeton Muslim community. The MSA shall strive to establish and maintain the Friday (Juma'a) prayers throughout the year, prayers and celebrations for both Eids, and iftaar (fast-break) meals during Ramadan. Additionally, the MSA shall make sure that there is a space on campus available for Muslim students to pray their daily prayers. Finally, the MSA shall do its best to increase unity within the Muslim community on campus through social events like study breaks, discussions, and dinners.
Section II
The secondary goal of the MSA is to serve the campus community. The MSA shall strive to enrich the diversity of campus life by educating our peers about the religion of Islam through lectures, events, dialogues, and similar events. Additionally, the MSA shall strive to create and participate in interfaith events that promote understanding and tolerance of the diverse religious traditions on campus.
mpu:53391.whatWeDo: We have awesome events and trips you can attend, with lots of free food!

mpu:53393.description: The OCF offers college students rich community in Christ, inspiring a life-long love of God and neighbor, and the POCF is here to do that on the Princeton University Campus! We hope to transform the lives of college students by guiding them along the path to Jesus Christ through His Church, cultivating a campus community of worship, witness, service, fellowship, and education.
mpu:53393.whatWeDo: We have on campus services weekly with a close spiritual community and clergy, fostering an environment composed of students, faculty, and outside residents alike. With our relationships and members, we often have presentations from guest speakers, visits from various archbishops, and collaborations with local parishes and other OCFs.
mpu:53393.goals:
1) to be the loving presence of Christ and the Orthodox Christian Church on college campuses
2) to be an integral part of students’ spiritual formation by challenging them to explore the Faith
3) to inspire students to commit to living an OrthodoxChristian way of life daily

mpu:53394.description: The Princeton Christian Fellowship is a non-denominational Christian campus ministry dedicated to teaching, serving, and building up students to live and love like Christ on Princeton's campus.

mpu:53395.tagline: Princeton's main student organization for Hindu life on campus

mpu:53397.description: Princeton Presbyterians welcomes all students into our beloved community to worship God in joy and hope and equip a new generation of Christian servant leaders.
mpu:53397.goals:
VALUE STATEMENTS
Hospitality–Because Christ welcomes all to the Lord’s Table, we welcome students from all walks of life. We celebrate people of all genders, sexualities, nationalities, ethnicities, and abilities as beloved children of God.
Social Justice–Because Scripture calls us to “do justice, love kindness, and walk humbly with God,”* we commit ourselves to the flourishing of all people and the restoration of creation through acts of service, public witness, and advocacy.
*Micah 6:8
Beloved Learning Community–Because God has made us members of Christ’s Body, we cultivate our hearts and minds through worship together and the study of Scripture. We equip a new generation of Christian servant-leaders with “energy, imagination, intelligence, and love."*
*Directory of Worship, W–4.0404h, Book of Order 2017–2019: The Constitution of the Presbyterian Church (U.S.A.) Part II (The Office of the General Assembly).
Joy & Hope–Because the Spirit gives us courage in a broken and fearful world,* we persevere in the truth that God’s Word is Good News for us and for the world. We proclaim in our words and actions that human value is not measured by performance or productivity, but in the steadfast love of the God who made us.
*A Brief Statement of Faith, 10.4, lines 65-66, The Book of Confessions: The Constitution of the Presbyterian Church (U.S.A.) Part I (The Office of the General Assembly).
Reformed–Because we are rooted in the Presbyterian Tradition, we cherish connections with the wider church in local congregations, the Presbytery of New Brunswick, the Synod of the Northeast, and the General Assembly of the PC(USA). Grounded in grace, we anticipate the ongoing movement of the Spirit in every season and respond with gratitude and continued reformation.

mpu:53401.description:
Princeton University Latter-Day Saints Student Association is an official student organization for those who are members of or have an interest in the Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints. In addition to providing support for the spiritual well-being of our members, LDSSA sponsors many activities within the university, with the local church organization of young adults, and with LDSSA groups from other universities.
Weekly church services, as of the 24-25 academic school year, are held on Sundays from 1:00 to 3:00 pm at the Latter-day Saint church building at 901 Canal Pointe Boulevard, just off campus. We carpool every Sunday and the outside of the building says "visitors welcome," so come join us!
Weekly Institute scripture study classes are also held on Tuesday evenings from 7:00 to 9:00 pm on-campus in Aaron Burr Hall 219.
Visitors are, again, more than welcome at either church or institute, and we also have regular social gatherings! To get connected and learn about other activities, send us an email at ldssa@princeton.edu :)

mpu:53403.description: To create an open space for members of the Sikh community to congregate (all are welcome).

mpu:53414.description: Outdoor Action (OA) is Princeton University's outdoor education and leadership development program. For over 45 years OA has served Princeton through the annual Frosh Trip outdoor orientation program for incoming first-year students, through the Leader Training program which trains current students to be leaders and role models to incoming students on the Frosh Trip, and alumni through on-campus events and outdoor-based adventure travel trips.
mpu:53414.whatWeDo: Outdoor Action trips and activities are open to all undergraduate students, graduate students, staff and faculty. There is no membership requirement.
mpu:53414.goals:
OA Mission Statement
To provide educational and character development experiences which advance personal responsibility, health and well-being, community, leadership development, civic engagement, and stewardship for Princeton and the natural world through adventure-based experiential education.

mpu:53451.description: The SAB of the Princeton University Art Museum is a group of undergraduate students dedicated to promoting an inclusive, accessible, and welcoming Museum space for the Princeton undergraduate community. Board members plan student events inspired by artwork in the Museum’s collections and collaborate with student groups and community partners to incorporate diverse voices into our programming. The board is committed to facilitating ongoing dialogues about equity, anti-racism, access, and inclusion in our work.

mpu:53482.description: Campus Recreation engages the Princeton University community in co-curricular experiences to inspire lifelong health and well-being.

mpu:53509.description: We are a large student organization dedicated to helping students explore a wider range of career opportunities, learn from professionals in the finance and consulting industries, and get connected with students sharing similar interests. We serve as an educational platform, organize speaker events, and facilitate conversations between students and professionals. We also aim to form long lasting alumni and corporate partnerships with interested firms.
mpu:53509.whatWeDo: Members get to participate in exclusive events with firms in the investment banking, asset management, private equity, venture capital, hedge fund, and consulting industries. Our partnership with firms allows members to build close professional relationships with alumni and campus recruiters across those industries. We also hold workshops that provide members with valuable knowledge in finance and business. We help students perfect their resumes, prepare for interviews, and navigate the finance and consulting recruiting process.

mpu:53780.description: A unit of the Office of the Dean of Undergraduate Students, PSA plays a pivotal role in the educational enterprise of Princeton, operating as a self-funded co-curricular program which exists to serve the University community.
mpu:53780.goals: Student Agencies is committed to providing undergraduates with unique opportunities in entrepreneurship through leadership of University-endorsed businesses, which support student and campus life at Princeton.

mpu:53789.description: The Aquinas Institute is your Catholic Campus Ministry at Princeton. Our mission is to fulfill the commission that Jesus gave us: “Go therefore and make disciples of all nations” (Matthew 28:19). We seek to share the love of God with all students, faculty and staff, because we believe that every person was created out of love by God and in the image of God, and therefore the only proper way to treat a person is with love.
mpu:53789.goals: Our goal is to provide for the spiritual, sacramental and pastoral needs of the Princeton community. We gather on campus for worship on Sundays at 4:30 and 10 pm for Mass, and during weekdays at 12 pm for daily Mass. We also provide opportunities for Confession, prayer, Adoration, Small Group Bible Studies, Discipleship formation, seminars, lectures, service, trips, retreats, and more.

mpu:53832.description: Vote100 is an intentional nonpartisan campus campaign aspiring for 100% of the undergraduate student body to engage civically. Our goal is to continue to highlight the critical importance of electoral participation as an essential aspect of a vibrant democracy; we want all members of our community to pledge to participate in all future elections, showing that civic responsibility is a foundational characteristic of what it means to be a Princetonian.

mpu:53879.description: Kindred Spirit was founded in 1991 by Dee Hausman in response to a vision God had placed in her heart to begin a Christian a cappella group on Princeton’s campus. Since then, KS has been offering inspirational outreach to the Princeton community and to our audiences everywhere through fellowship, arch sings, gospel jams, community service, and shared testimonies.
mpu:53879.goals: We are devoted to spreading the gospel through song, to encouraging one another as brothers and sisters in Christ, and to glorifying the name of Jesus Christ.

mpu:55462.description: Coptic Society is an organization that offers students a spiritual supplement to the secularity of academia. It is an organization which looks to center itself on Christ and hopes to support the surrounding community by embodying the spirit of the Church on campus. Members are encouraged to integrate their beliefs as Christians into their lives as students by promoting tolerance and fellowship. This organization is neither restricted to a singular race nor particular religion.

mpu:55463.description: ASAP is a group where Asian student-athletes can connect and celebrate their Asian identities and the role of these identities in life as student-athletes. ASAP strives to foster a safe and welcoming community to promote conversations about race and identity, and provide support to Asian student-athletes, but also hosts fun events for members to enjoy. The group also connects current members with alumni for mentorship opportunities and guest speaker events. The goal is to create a platform for Asian student-athletes to share their personal experiences and feel heard while being inspired and guided by Asian former student-athletes. ASAP is open to all student-athletes.

mpu:55715.description: The ASCE Princeton Chapter is open to all students interested in civil and environmental engineering professions. The goals of ASCE are to foster a welcoming environment within CEE, to encourage peer-to-peer academic support, and to provide opportunities for professional development within the field.

mpu:56464.description:
To provide a space for Princeton students and other community members interested in Quantum Information Science (QIS).
To facilitate student participation in external quantum hackathons, challenges, and other competitions.
To identify opportunities for and organize trips to quantum research facilities, conferences, and guest speakers.
To foster community between students, faculty, and alum interested in QIS and form a network of contacts in academia and industry.
To aid students in learning about quantum development, quantum information science theory, and quantum machine learning by compiling resources and hosting events (quantum challenges, hackathons, guest speakers).
To contribute to open source quantum development libraries (ex. qiskit, pennylane).
mpu:56464.goals:
To provide a space for Princeton students and other community members interested in Quantum Information Science (QIS).
To facilitate student participation in external quantum hackathons, challenges, and other competitions.
To identify opportunities for and organize trips to quantum research facilities, conferences, and guest speakers.
To foster community between students, faculty, and alum interested in QIS and form a network of contacts in academia and industry.
To aid students in learning about quantum development, quantum information science theory, and quantum machine learning by compiling resources and hosting events (quantum challenges, hackathons, guest speakers).
To contribute to open source quantum development libraries (ex. qiskit, pennylane ).

mpu:56468.description: The Black Student-Athlete Collective (BSAC) at Princeton University is an organization dedicated to fostering community, empowerment, and advocacy for Black student-athletes on campus. It provides a supportive network where Black athletes can connect, share experiences, and discuss challenges unique to their identities as both students and athletes. The collective often hosts events, workshops, and discussions focused on issues such as racial equity, mental health, and career development, all within the context of athletics. Additionally, BSAC works to promote inclusivity and representation in Princeton's athletic programs, ensuring that the voices and perspectives of Black student-athletes are heard and valued. Through its initiatives, BSAC aims to create a more equitable and supportive environment for Black athletes at Princeton.

mpu:56720.description: The Chinese Language Association (CLA) has a fundamental mission: to bring together the community of Chinese language learners and native speakers to foster a safe environment to practice Mandarin and appreciate Chinese culture. To achieve this, CLA hosts events from mahjong nights to KungFu Panda watch parties to provide opportunities to practice speaking Chinese and connect over culture, and food. Events including game nights, calligraphy lessons, and study breaks, as well as collaborations with other campus groups and academic departments, are anticipated for this semester.

mpu:56763.description: Campus Life enhances the holistic development and educational experience for all students by complementing academic study with co-curricular opportunities that engage, enrich and advance student learning and growth.
mpu:56763.goals: Campus Life strives to provide an integrated educational experience that cultivates skills and habits of mind that inspires students to lead lives of meaning, purpose, and social responsibility.

mpu:56983.description: The John H. Pace, Jr. '39 Center for Civic Engagement makes make service and civic engagement a central part of the Princeton student experience so that undergraduate and graduate students can respond to the needs of the world in responsible ways.
mpu:56983.goals:
We prepare undergraduate and graduate students to serve well by making meaningful connections through learning, experience, and reflection. Helping students discover service through connecting with each other and communities that they care about creates a strong foundation for understanding what it means to be an engaged citizen. It is our vision that Princeton University students will make the world more equitable, creating access and opportunity for all people and communities to thrive.
We are located at: Frist Campus Center, Room 201D and 58 Prospect Avenue, Third Floor.

mpu:58778.description: Princeton University's Mixed Association aims to foster a vibrant and inclusive community for undergraduates by promoting awareness and understanding of mixed-race and other mixed identities and experiences. Through our social gatherings, open dialogues, and joint programming with other cultural clubs, we strive to enrich campus life and support the unique perspectives and voices of mixed-race students.

mpu:58950.description: The CST is comprised of dedicated faculty and staff who work to advance STEM literacy across Princeton University and beyond through rigorous course development, creative interdisciplinary programming, and robust educational research. By developing strong collaborations across disciplines, the CST seeks to ensure that all members of the Princeton University community, regardless of their background, experience, or discipline, can engage with, appreciate, and apply science in their everyday lives, in their careers, and in society.

mpu:59878.description: The Graduate School works to ensure that your Princeton experience is both personally and academically rewarding by developing events, resources and services to support your needs. At Princeton, we connect across interests of all kinds. All events and programs run by the Graduate School and by student organizations are open to all Princeton University students, regardless of identity, such as race, sex, ethnicity, national origin, or other protected characteristics.

mpu:61570.tagline: Enabling high-impact research by bringing education and advanced computing to the Princeton community.
mpu:61570.description:
Princeton Research Computing, a collaborative effort led by Research Computing, the Princeton Institute for Computational Science and Engineering (PICSciE), and other campus partners, welcomes and encourages participation from faculty in all academic departments.
Computational modeling and analysis has firmly established itself as the third pillar of scientific research, while at the same time the humanities and social sciences have been relying increasingly on information technology to carry out research. Princeton has positioned itself well to excel in this new era, building a centralized infrastructure to support the faculty and researchers with their increasing computational and digital data needs.
Our centralized infrastructure and services are used by most academic departments, and we have built a community welcoming staff and researchers from departments that provide some or all of their own research computing infrastructure and support. The goal of our program is to provide the infrastructure and support that meet the needs and priorities of our faculty, researchers, and students.
Our comprehensive program addresses many facets of research computing including:
Education, Training & Outreach: Graduate certificate in computational science & engineering, mini-courses, workshops, seminars, and conferences.
Services: System administration, programming, research software engineering, cloud computing, and secure research infrastructure.
Systems: High-Performance Computing (HPC) clusters and large memory servers and data storage systems for data ranging from working data sets on our computational resources to persistent published data.

mpu:61730.tagline: Enabling research, teaching and communication at Princeton
mpu:61730.description:
The mission of OIT is to enable the effective use of information technology in support of the University. Our primary focus is on providing information technology products and services that meet the needs of the Princeton community and achieve the highest level of customer satisfaction.
OIT has responsibility for overseeing Princeton’s academic and administrative systems and the information technology infrastructure that supports them. We are proud of the fact that Princeton is widely seen as a leader in providing a robust infrastructure for campus computing and in identifying and deploying new technologies that enable academic innovation in teaching, learning, research, and scholarship.
OIT strives to enable communication and collaboration among information technology professionals and users of information technology at Princeton. OIT staff are committed to supporting all members of the University in their academic and administrative work.
Please enjoy your visit to the OIT website. Here, you can learn about the IT products and services available to students, faculty, and staff and how it can facilitate the work you are doing.

mpu:61803.description:
We are an Executive Board of 13 graduate students and an Assembly of 50+ graduate students, representing all academic departments and various student interest groups. Our executive board members are elected by the entire graduate student body, and we meet weekly to discuss various initiatives, priorities, and campus collaborations. Our Assembly representatives are elected by their academic departments or student interest groups, and meet monthly to discuss issues brought forward by their constituents.
Our mission is to support and advocate for graduate students in their multiple roles: as researchers, as teachers, as students, and as members of the broader Princeton University community. We work directly with University administrators and deans to make sure grad students’ voices are heard: we are the graduate community’s mouthpiece to the University administration. We also work year-round to foster a positive, inclusive, and engaged grad student community.
We advocate for graduate students’ needs by: fighting for grad students’ financial, healthcare, and housing protections; collaborating with University offices on professional development opportunities; sponsoring mental health and wellness events all year round; investigating and addressing teaching load and other graduate labor inequities; promoting transparency in all University policies and procedures; and advocating on behalf of any grad student who seeks our support.
We foster community by: running a University-wide Slack community of 2,000+ Princeton grad students; sending a weekly newsletter highlighting news and events of interest to grad students; hosting weekly graduate student Happy Hours; co-organizing the Grad Student Buddy Program for new grad students; and planning special events and themed parties all year round!

mpu:61804.description: To advocate for Lakeside residents. Our committee acts as a liason between Lakeside residents and officials at the university and American Campus Communities.

mpu:61806.description:
SACNAS fosters the success of Hispanic/Chicano, Native American, and minority scientists, from college students to professionals, by:
-Encouraging and supporting undergraduates, graduate students, postdocs, and professionals in pursuing and attaining advanced degrees, careers, and positions of leadership in the STEM fields.
-Enhancing public understanding, awareness, and appreciation for Chicanos, Latinos, Native Americans, African Americans, and other underrepresented minorities in the STEM fields.
-Informing and advocating public policies and governmental funding that supports the advancement of Hispanics/Chicanos, Native Americans, African Americans, and other minorities and to the building of a large and diverse U.S. STEM workforce.
**All undergraduates, graduate students, postdocs, and professionals who identify as underrepresented in STEM and/or supporters of promoting the success of individuals from diverse backgrounds in STEM are welcome to all SACNAS-sponsored programming**

mpu:61807.description: The Princeton University Graduate Consulting Club (PUGCC) enables our members across all disciplines and backgrounds with opportunities in consulting as a means to an alternative career. We provide access to professional development resources, as well as consulting opportunities to build foundational skills and gain critical experience. Noteworthy features of the PUGCC include volunteer consulting initiatives, case study practice sessions and invitational seminar series featuring experts in the field.

mpu:61809.description: We are a student organization aiming to serve the Chinese community at Princeton and to provide help with their daily life, academic study, and career needs. During each school year, ACSSPU hosts a variety of social, cultural, and intellectual events for Chinese students and scholars at Princeton. Please follow us on Facebook (@acssputiger) and Instagram (@princeton_acsspu), where you can find the most up-to-date information about ACSSPU. You can contact us at acsspu@princeton.edu.

mpu:61810.description: The Association of South Asians at Princeton holds events throughout the year to foster community here on campus. All are welcome!

mpu:61811.description:
Our organization organizes and hosts events for graduate students celebrating Canadian culture and identity at Princeton, including Thanksgiving dinner, a Canada Day barbecue, a May 2-4 party and other gatherings to celebrate quintessential Canadian holidays and foster a Canadophile community at Princeton.
Notre association rassemble les étudiantes et étudiants aux études supérieures de Princeton avec divers événements célébrant la culture canadienne, y compris un souper de l'Action de grâce, un barbecue pour le jour du déménagement (autrement appelé la fête du Canada), un party pour la Journée nationale des patriotes (et aussi la reine Victoria) et quoi que ce soit qui fait partie de la culture canadienne et cultive la communauté canadophile à Princeton.

mpu:61815.goals: Our guiding goal is to provide the highest quality yoga instruction at a price that's affordable for graduate students. We seek out great instructors to teach each of our classes. Our classes are in the alignment-focused Iyengar tradition. With the help of our volunteer organizers, costs are kept low, in part through a system of pre-payment for the 12-20 week sessions. Space in the classes is always limited, and demand always exceeds our capacity. As such, we do our best to accommodate as many yogis as possible. This organization is open to all Princeton University students interested in supporting our organization’s mission, regardless of identity, such as race, sex, ethnicity, national origin, or other protected characteristics.

mpu:61819.description: The Graduate Engineering Council (GEC) at Princeton University works as a liaison between the School of Engineering and Applied Sciences graduate student body and the administration, serving to keep graduate students informed about the decisions and forthcoming projects currently being discussed by the administration, while the representatives from each department bring the problems and concerns of graduate students to the attention of the administration to work toward a solution. The GEC also provides interactive and informative programs for our 600+ graduate engineering students.

mpu:61824.description:
GradSWE aims to foster a community of inclusion and empowerment among
women and minority graduate students specifically in the engineering and
sciences. Our organization and events are open to all genders and all majors!
We focus on building community through social activities, mentoring and
outreach with undergraduates and beyond, and professional development.

mpu:61826.description: Online publication at Princeton U. on topics related to sustainable development. Contributions from the University community, managed by graduate students.
mpu:61826.goals:
This publication has two goals:
1) to provide a space for members of the University community to write about how their work contributes to the goal of sustainable development; and
2) to accommodate multiple perspectives from across the University community by bringing together contributions from across academic disciplines. You can read more about the blog's vision in the Introduction by The Editorial Board: https://highwire.princeton.edu/2015/12/16/andsowerise/

mpu:61830.description:
We spend time together finding answers to life’s biggest questions: about meaning, purpose, pain, significance, existence, God. We’re a community open to all Princeton students, regardless of their spiritual background.
This organization is open to all Princeton University students interested in supporting our organization’s mission, regardless of identity, such as race, sex, ethnicity, national origin, or other protected characteristics.
mpu:61830.whatWeDo: We eat a lot of food together, we go kayaking, hiking, we go on fun trips, and we play lots of games together: sports, boardgames, trivia games, you name it. And, in whatever circumstance in life, COVID or not, we’re a community: we support each other, and we do "life" together. Come with as many questions as you like about life, religion, Christianity, God, the Bible, or Jesus – we're here for them all.
mpu:61830.goals: All of us in Campus Light came from different backgrounds – atheism, Buddhism, agnosticism, Christianity, etc. But we all converged when we were looking for answers to those deep, 2-AM questions and for a community that would accept us without pretenses. Our goal is to lower barriers to finding answers for the deeper questions you've been pondering, and our goal is to make that happen in community.

mpu:61833.description:
LGSA aims to promote the academic, social, and professional well-being of Latino/Hispanic graduate students at Princeton. LGSA strives to render visible issues that are relevant to the Hispanic/Latino community at large. As America's largest and most diverse minority group, Latinos have faced varied and complex obstacles in their efforts to achieve educational excellence. Social circumstances have often inhibited Latino interest in both undergraduate and, particularly, graduate programs. The members of LGSA aspire to implement a multi-dimensional program of support for students at all levels of the academy. LGSA will provide a space for graduate students to establish a community by offering opportunities for dialogue, exchange, and support at Princeton.
**This organization is open to all Princeton University students interested in supporting our organization regardless of identity, such as race, sex, ethnicity, national origin, or other protected characteristics**

mpu:61837.description: The Princeton African Graduate Students Association (PAGSA) aims to develop a thriving community for African students at Princeton through social, academic, and professional programming
mpu:61837.goals: Minimum of three general audience meetings: 1) Meet & Greet Dinner, 2) Late Night Dance Party, 3) Career and Alumni Discussion

mpu:61844.description: We are a group of Princeton students across the university who are determined to promote incorporating science into policy-making and advocate for the advanced of science education and communication. We’ve been organizing since the November 2016 election to understand what we, as scientists and scholars, can do to tackle the societal issues we face today and to promote democratic participation and evidence-based policy-making.
mpu:61844.whatWeDo: During the year, we host a scientific communication workshop (open to all!), and work in smaller committees throughout the year to organize events. Previous events include the Princeton Day of Action, and writing to congressional members.

mpu:61845.description:
Effective altruism is a philosophy and movement focused on using evidence and careful reasoning to maximise the good you can do through your career, projects, and donations.
At Princeton Effective Altruism, we are driven to solve the largest problems that humanity faces today—whether it be global health, extreme poverty, animal welfare, engineered pandemics, AI risk, nuclear security, climate change, or other existential and global catastrophic risks—through research, public policy, ethics, charity entrepreneurship, philanthropy, direct work, and the many other resources, opportunities and privileges at our disposal.

mpu:61847.tagline: For all enthusiasts of Polish culture!
mpu:61847.description: The Princeton Polish Society seeks to foster a Polish community on campus and give students space to interact with the diversity of Polish culture, cuisine, and language. While many of the society's members are of Polish origin, we are equally welcoming to all enthusiasts of Poland and those curious to discover its cultural richness. This organization is open to all Princeton University students interested in supporting our organization’s mission, regardless of identity, such as race, sex, ethnicity, national origin, or other protected characteristics.

mpu:61851.description:
We are a pickup soccer group open to all skill levels. The group mostly consists of graduate students and post-docs, but other university affiliates are more than welcome!
We typically play twice a week. Please use the following link to add yourself to the listserv and stay informed: https://lists.princeton.edu/cgi-bin/wa?SUBED1=gradfc&A=1. There will be one email per week detailing the location, times, and rules--we generally will not be using MyPrincetonU, so please be sure to join the listserv if you are interested!

mpu:61853.description:
Dear Undergrads, Grad Students, Faculty, and Staff, welcome to the Princeton Tango Club!
Join us and share the joy of Argentine Tango with the Princeton community. Learn tango in our
- Weekly classes (Mondays)
- Guided Practicas (Sundays)
- Events and social dancing activities
Check our calendar at https://www.princetontangoclub.com/event-calendar/
Our classes are beginner-friendly throughout the year, so do not fear to join us any time. No partner, experience, or material necessary to attend, although you will appreciate wearing flexible and slippery shoes. Nevertheless, ask us for dancing socks at the beginning of the class if you feel like your shoes are not "slippery enough". Classes are led by our incredible instructors Sean Ericson, Jacqueline Pham, Amelia Foss, and Miloš Nikolić.
See you on Monday!

mpu:61861.description: Women in Chemistry at Princeton University is a network of undergraduate students, graduate students, postdoctoral fellows, faculty, and staff dedicated to supporting and promoting women in chemistry. Through social events, discussions with visiting seminar speakers at “FaculTea” and “DiversiTea” events, as well as professional development workshops, we hope to strengthen the community of and support system between women chemists. We also hope to increase the visibility of women in STEM, become involved in the local community, and encourage young women to pursue STEM careers through involvement in outreach and mentorship programs.

mpu:61863.description: The Women in STEM Leadership Council is comprised of the leaders of various department women in STEM groups on campus and is convened by the Graduate School Diversity and Inclusion team. At present, we have members from the following departments: Applied and Computational Math, Architecture, Astrophysics, Chemistry, Civil and Environmental Engineering, Computer Science, Ecology and Evolutionary Biology, Mechanical Engineering, and Physics. Our events are open to all Princeton University graduate students regardless of gender identity.
mpu:61863.goals:
The goal of the council is to tackle problems graduate women in STEM face. Some work we have done include:
Conducted our own campus climate surveys (2015 and 2018), collecting experiences of the graduate women in STEM fields at Princeton and combining the results into a report presented to the university administration.
Hosted a Women in STEM symposium to discuss some of the past and present trends of women in the STEM fields.
Invited acclaimed scientists to address the Princeton community in public seminars.
Held regular networking and mentoring events for Women in STEM fields at Princeton.
Reviewed and provided feedback on several training modules on sexual discrimination and harassment.

mpu:61864.description:
Princeton Zen Club strives to build an inclusive community for active mindfulness practices. We serve as a platform for all Princeton members to learn and advance in meditation through guided meditation classes and on-campus events.
We draw inspiration from Zen Buddhism to reduce stress, increase focus & productivity, and enhance our overall well-being. All backgrounds and beliefs are welcome!
This organization is open to all Princeton University students interested in supporting our organization’s mission, regardless of identity, such as race, sex, ethnicity, national origin, or other protected characteristics.

mpu:61869.description:
Womxn in Design and Architecture (WDA) is a graduate student group formed at Princeton University School of Architecture (SoA) in 2014 to highlight womxn through academic programming and lecture series.
WDA is committed to offering an intersectional platform for architectural discourse. Bringing attention to issues of equity, including gender, class, and race disparities, WDA encourages new standards of recognition and representation within both academic and professional settings.
Beginning in 2017, the annual conference, organized by WDA and Princeton SoA, celebrates the unwritten or underexplored histories of architects such as Anne Tyng, Norma Merrick Sklarek, Lina Bo Bardi, and Zaha Hadid.

mpu:61944.tagline: The Lewis Center for the Arts encompasses the Programs in Creative Writing, Dance, Theater, Music Theater, Visual Arts including Film, and the Princeton Atelier.
mpu:61944.description:
At the Lewis Center for the Arts, we believe that art arises out of questions. Art, on a campus like Princeton, is so much more than an outlet for expressing what one already knows and feels, or an escape hatch for blowing off steam built up by more rigorous kinds of work. Our classes and minor programs in Dance, Creative Writing, Theater & Music Theater, Visual Arts and in the interdisciplinary Princeton Atelier operate on the principle that rigorous artistic practice is a form of research, innovation, discovery and intervention. Like scholarship of any kind, rigorous artistic practice is a way of interrogating that which is accepted or understood in an attempt to break into the territory of the unknown or under-explored.
Through their individual creative work, Lewis Center students investigate questions about themselves, others, and the events and systems that affect us all systems like geography, politics, gender, race, the economy, the environment, and of course the wide realm of human choice and activity. This is fundamental to the formation of artists. It is also fundamental to the formation of alert, compassionate, creative, resourceful, and active rather than passive people.
The Lewis Center is committed to being an anti-racist space. We endeavor to frequently reappraise and redouble our efforts toward this goal. Our commitment to diversity and inclusion is not nominal or symbolic, but rather action-based. Our faculty, classes, public programs, co-curricular offerings and our engagement with the community beyond Princeton reflect these values.

mpu:61947.description: The Program for Community-Engaged Scholarship (ProCES) fosters relationships that bring community-identified priorities and interests into conversation with academic learning goals. ProCES courses integrate community-engaged teaching, an experiential learning pedagogy in which faculty and students collaborate with community partners and non-academic experts. Engagement takes a variety of forms, including: community-based research, empirical analysis, service learning, citizen science, participant observation, public humanities, practicing arts, and other collaborative modalities and methods of knowledge co-creation.

mpu:62016.description:
The Website Wednesday meeting is intended for anyone who produces, maintains, edits, designs, or develops websites at Princeton University. No technical background is necessary to benefit from this event.
We focus on the centrally supported website platforms while looking to be inclusive of all digital publishing needs across the University.
Topics are proposed and voted on by the group members.
The meeting is held one Wednesday per month during the academic year. Our typical meeting format is a 45-60 minute presentation followed by an informal 30-minutes for the website community to connect, share ideas, and support one another.

mpu:62058.description: The Office of Religious Life supports all members of the Princeton community, of any religious identity or of none, in answering for themselves their own questions of how to find meaning and how to live.
mpu:62058.goals:
The Office of Religious Life at Princeton University values
Radical Welcome
We serve the entire Princeton community. All are welcome at our programs and in our spaces, whether or not they hold specific religious beliefs or want to explore different religious or spiritual traditions.
Spiritual Exploration
We lean into big questions of meaning and purpose, and we assert that spiritual exploration can be an important pathway to finding individual answers.
Diversity
We affirm that there is much to be learned by sharing space, conversation, and experiences with people of diverse backgrounds, beliefs, and life paths. We uphold the radically equal value of each person’s identities.
Community
We bring people together for ritual and celebration— in sangha, fellowship, and jama’a. We offer presence and care when people are struggling, when they are rejoicing, and everything in between.
Engagement
We work to form educated, articulate, compassionate, other-aware citizens who participate in critical issues of human flourishing and peace building in our region, country, and world.
