mpu:62663.description: The Program in American Studies – home to the programs in Asian American studies and Latino studies – studies America in the world and the world in America.

mpu:64344.description:
The mission of the Gender + Sexuality Resource Center (GSRC) is to foster a supportive and inclusive campus community that affirms women, fem, trans, and queer Princetonians. We achieve this goal by offering collaborative programming, education, advocacy, mentorship, and wellness initiatives that are open to all Princeton undergraduate and graduate students.
We envision a Princeton University community of practice that uplifts and celebrates women, fem, trans, and queer people and that actively resists sexism, cissexism, heteronormativity and other intersecting forms of oppression on campus and beyond.
mpu:64344.goals:
Our Center’s Core Values:
We approach our work with a historical and intersectional analysis of discrimination and injustice to intentionally and equitably serve our campus community
We center the philosophy that there is no one way to be a woman, fem, queer, and/or trans person at Princeton
We recognize that everyone is at a different place in their learning process; thus, we actively embrace and support differences to authentically engage
We develop and sustain intentional partnerships, both inside and outside the university, to make our work more effective and impactful
We center the joy, care, and well-being of women, fem, queer, and trans communities in all of our programming, education, and advocacy initiatives

mpu:64853.description: The Financial Literacy Initiative empowers students with the resources, tools and knowledge to cultivate financial wellness during their time at Princeton and beyond.

mpu:65124.description: Giving graduate students the tools to make informed decisions about spending, banking, budgeting, and credit.
mpu:65124.whatWeDo: Be the first to learn about programs offered by the Graduate School and the Financial Literacy Initiative.

mpu:65233.description: Princeton Star Wars Club is an inclusive and friendly community for members to share their love of all things Star Wars! We hold watch parties for new and existing media and facilitate book clubs, gaming sessions, trivia nights and more.

mpu:65241.description:
The Princeton University Balkan Society proclaims that it has been founded and is
dedicated to promote and encourage, amongst its members:
1. To promote and share Balkan culture and history
2. To provide a space for students of Balkan heritage to connect and meet with one
another, celebrate a shared heritage, and foster mutual respect
3. To create an open space for student of all backgrounds to learn more about the
Balkans via cultural events
On campus, we would like to introduce the broader Princeton community to the rich Balkan culture and tradition. Today’s eastern Europe is a neglected region of the world that is primarily known for its conflicts, particularly within the Balkans. We as an organization would like to foster ideals of unity and community among students of Balkan descent to stem these negative associations with the region.

mpu:65243.description: We encourage and promote a stress-free environment where members can form a tight-knit community and create new connections with others through a common, shared activity. We want to introduce people to the world of yarn crafts and to encourage the growth of this hobby that has shown to be effective in improving mental health and reducing stress & anxiety levels. We hope to crochet and knit garments in need for those in need in Mercer County in an effort to give back to the surrounding community. We aim to provide a place for members to express their artistic creativity in a judgement-free zone, where everyone is accepted.

mpu:65290.description: To introduce Princetonians to the blockchain ecosystem and actively contribute to the space.

mpu:65408.description: SoA Radio is a live, ongoing, experimental radio station run by students of the School of Architecture at Princeton University. We started up during the pandemic and have the ability to run 24/7, and are interested in using the medium of radio to explore student and faculty interests in architecture, art, music, and culture. Many of the shows focus on music and conversations relating to architecture and space, while others shows explore other student interests like identity, media, and storytelling. All architecture students and professors are invited to have shows. In the past year, the radio station has provided community and interaction for remote and faraway students. We hope to keep connecting our small student body. We hope to hold events in the fall now that we can all meet in person to listen to music, silkscreen fabric with the radio logo, and share meals.

mpu:65409.description: The Princeton University Neurodiversity Collective (PUNC) empowers Princeton’s self-identifying neurodiverse students, faculty, post-docs, and staff, by building supportive communities, engaging in advocacy, fostering positive newfound visibility, and arming the neurodiverse community with tools for professional and personal success. We strive to acknowledge and rectify persistent ableist inequalities and to increase awareness of the Princeton campus community’s neurodiverse population. PUNC welcomes and celebrates all cognitive identities with or without a specific diagnosis. Membership: Open to all self identifying neurodiverse students, post-docs, faculty, staff.

mpu:65411.description: SPIA Latinx provides a safe and welcoming space for SPIA's growing robust and diverse Latinx community. It gives students the opportunity to discuss policy issues that impact the Latinx community, both domestically and internationally, with one another or with an invited speaker. As an affinity group, we will also have bonding events, to help form a sense of community.

mpu:65643.description: The Graduate Princeton Quantum Computing (GPQC) club will work closely with the undergraduate branch (Princeton Quantum Computing) to create a community of quantum scientists, engineers and enthusiasts at Princeton University. Particularly, this branch will ensure graduate interaction and participation in Princeton's quantum computing community.
mpu:65643.goals:
The following initiatives are examples of what GPQC encourages and promotes for its members:
To provide a space for Princeton students and other community members interested in Quantum Information Science (QIS).
To facilitate student participation in external quantum hackathons, challenges, and other competitions.
To identify opportunities for and organize trips to quantum research facilities, conferences, and guest speakers.
To foster community between students, faculty, and alum interested in QIS and form a network of contacts in academia and industry.
To aid students in learning about quantum development, quantum information science theory, and quantum machine learning by compiling resources and hosting events (quantum challenges, hackathons, guest speakers).
To contribute to open source quantum development libraries (ex. qiskit, pennylane ).

mpu:65644.description: The Colombian Studies Group serves as a center to promote interdisciplinary debates in Princeton regarding Colombia, the surrounding region, and its diaspora abroad, through cultural promotion, environmental discussions, academic collaboration, and civic education. We host events with researchers, policymakers, and activists of interest to the Colombian community in Princeton, as well as the broader student body interested in the region's affairs.

mpu:66080.description:
Our mission is to build the world's fastest electric boats, pushing the limits of electric propulsion and promoting sustainability in marine transportation.
This organization is open to all Princeton University students interested in supporting our organization’s mission, regardless of identity, such as race, sex, ethnicity, national origin, or other protected characteristics.
mpu:66080.goals: We design and build electrically powered race boats from the ground up by tackling the various aspects of the engineering process, namely mechanical, electrical, and cooling systems.

mpu:66167.description: Kalaa is Princeton’s premier South Asian classical dance troupe. Our mission is to keep alive heritage and traditional dances while sharing their cultural vibrancy with our community.
mpu:66167.whatWeDo:
- A dedicated community for celebrating classical dance and South Asian culture
- Opportunity to interact with renowned artists

mpu:66188.description: The Princeton University OPTICA Chapter provides its members with professional networking, career development, and technical programming. The chapter works to raise awareness of optics and photonics through participation in events at Princeton University and in the local community through youth education outreach activities such as science fairs, lab tours and classroom demonstrations. Biweekly journal club meetings are hosted by graduate students to discuss current progress and trends in the field of optical science.

mpu:66577.description: The Graduate Women of Color Caucus encourages graduate women of color from all disciplines to come together for professional development, mentoring, and networking to address issues of interest to our community. The caucus holds monthly meetings and seminars to discuss the unique challenges women of color encounter and specific ways to successfully navigate the academy.

mpu:66673.description: As a student-led society and Friend of MSF, we strive to educate both the immediate Princeton University community and the communities around us to raise awareness about the important medical and humanitarian work and wide-reaching effects of MSF.

mpu:66683.description: The Women in Medicine Club is dedicated to creating an inclusive, supportive community for students interested in pursuing medical careers. Our mission is to empower members through educational and enrichment opportunities, fostering personal and professional growth. We aim to address gender disparities in the health professions by offering mentorship, facilitating critical discussions, and organizing hands-on experiences. By building strong connections and inspiring the next generation of medical leaders, we strive to uplift each other and promote diversity in the medical field.

mpu:66752.description:
A group dedicated to Chinese dance for the love of dance. Grounded in
classical Chinese dance, this group wishes to build a fun and nurturing
environment where students get a chance to explore the creative side of
cross-cultural fusion while learning traditional Chinese dance grammar and
technique.
Participants will meet one or two times per week. Practice
includes Chinese classical dance/folk dance techniques and basic ballet
workouts. One or two performances are expected to be done every
semester.
This organization is open to all Princeton University students interested in supporting our organization’s mission, regardless of identity, such as race, sex, ethnicity, national origin, or other protected characteristics.

mpu:66860.description:
At the Fields Center, diverse perspectives and experiences of race, class, gender and their intersections are supported and challenged, questioned and answered.
These values are cultivated through the celebration of heritage months, dialogues and discussions, our Princeton University Mentoring Program (PUMP) and the Fields Fellows peer educator program. Additionally, our Center’s student friendly space offers numerous opportunities for relaxation and engagement – comfy lounges, study breaks, movie nights, galas, festivals and more.
mpu:66860.goals:
We work to empower, engage, and educate individuals and institutions within the University community to develop, implement and support systems of inclusion.
Pillars: Engagement. Empowerment. Leadership. Action.

mpu:66880.description: Our mission is to provide opportunities and a dedicated space specifically for Princeton students interested in dental careers. We aim to foster a supportive community that encourages professional development, knowledge sharing, and networking among students passionate about the field of dentistry.

mpu:67099.description: Princeton University is committed to equal opportunity and non-discrimination. To maximize excellence, we seek talent from all segments of American society and the world, and we take steps to ensure everyone at Princeton can thrive while they are here. That is the sole rationale and purpose of our diversity and inclusion programs, all of which are voluntary and open to all, and which comply with federal and state non-discrimination laws. Princeton does not discriminate on the basis of race, sex, ethnicity, color, national origin, religion, disability, or any other protected characteristic, and Princeton does not provide special benefits or preferential treatment on the basis of a protected characteristic.
mpu:67099.whatWeDo: Learn more about our exciting signature program events for GSP, our Diversity Fellows, and our Affinity Student Orgs!
mpu:67099.goals: The Graduate School works to ensure that your Princeton experience is both personally and academically rewarding by developing events, resources and services to support your needs. At Princeton, we connect across interests of all kinds. All events and programs run by the Graduate School and by student organizations are open to all Princeton University students, regardless of identity, such as race, sex, ethnicity, national origin, or other protected characteristics.

mpu:67103.description: The Princeton University Muslim Engineers for Social Impact and Justice (MESIJ) is a student organization at Princeton University dedicated to thinking about and engaging with social impact and justice matters through engineering from an Islamic framework.

mpu:67103.goals:
As a student organization, and a broader collective we hope to:
- Provide a safe and inclusive environment to discuss the intersection of technology and humanity
- Learn and shed light on technological injustice and how it impacts global Muslim communities
- Ideate ways in which we can give back to our community through engineering and collaboration
- Congregate with fellow Muslim engineers both at Princeton and in industry to establish a sense of community and representation in the engineering world

mpu:67157.description:
To maintain a Ukrainian presence on campus by engaging in activism, cultural diplomacy, and community outreach, as well as creating a space for Ukrainians on campus to connect.

mpu:67251.description: Welcome to MakeNet! We're a community of Princeton students, staff, faculty, and alumni who make things and want to talk about making things. Here you'll find opportunities to share your projects, ask for help, and learn more about engineering and artistic practice.

mpu:67263.description: National Alzheimer’s Buddies is an intergenerational movement responding to the profound isolation and social disengagement experienced by people in the intermediate-to-late stages of Alzheimer’s disease (AD). Through partnering college volunteers with residents (buddies) at memory care facilities, we build meaningful, lasting relationships that break through the boundaries imposed by Alzheimer’s disease. Learn more at our instagram @alzbuddies_princeton
mpu:67263.whatWeDo:
Fun Events and Activities:
- Weekly 1:1 in-person volunteer sessions at local memory care facility (transportation provided)
- Guest speakers who will speak about the caregiving experience or Alzheimer’s disease research
- Campus-wide Alzheimer’s disease advocacy and fundraising opportunities
- A lifetime's worth of lessons and memories from interacting with your buddy!
mpu:67263.goals: Through one on one visits, volunteers and buddies build meaningful relationships with one another all while reducing the emotional burden of Alzheimer’s on both the individuals with the disease as well as families and caretakers.

mpu:67347.description: To create a community for premedical students at Princeton and provide opportunities for education, mentorship, and collaboration.

mpu:67393.description: AI@Princeton is the largest undergraduate AI community at Princeton, with over 300 active members. Our mission is to empower undergrads to engage in cutting-edge AI research and engineering. We host weekly research talks and professor Q&As to expand AI literacy for the broader Princeton community. Our flagship event is AI TigerTrek, an annual trip to SF for students to connect with researchers, startups, VCs, and academics working at the frontier of AI.

mpu:67396.description:
A new publishing press run by Princeton students, for Princeton students. Dedicated to empowering students in publishing their work, giving their stories a home, amplifying emerging and underrepresented voices on campus, and strengthening the campus community.
Staff and manuscript applications will open fall of 2025. We are looking for writing editors, artists, social media managers, and web designers!

mpu:67529.description:
The Developmental Biology Colloquium is a weekly, student-organized seminar series that highlights the work of graduate students and postdocs from across departments and exposes attendees to new and diverse developmental biology research via invited talks.
The developmental biology community at Princeton brings together labs from Molecular Biology, Chemical and Biological Engineering, Ecology and Evolutionary Biology, and the Lewis Sigler Institute for Genetics and Genomics. The Developmental Biology Colloquium is well attended by graduate students, post-doctoral fellows, and faculty. The weekly seminar presents a valuable opportunity for graduate students to share their work and gain critical feedback. Our colloquium seeks to have representation from both early and late-stage graduate students via short, in-progress talks from second and third year graduate students and longer, formal presentations from fourth and fifth year graduate students preparing to defend and go on the job market.
mpu:67529.whatWeDo: In addition to talks from members of the Princeton community, Developmental Biology Colloquium invites speakers based on suggestions from our attendees. We seek to highlight diverse speakers from different institutions, stages of career, and scientific background. Following invited speakers’ talks, they meet with graduate students/members and post-docs to discuss science and their career paths, which helps trainees to forge larger connections with the developmental biology community.
mpu:67529.goals: Devbio aims to give graduate students a critical platform to have their research heard any the community as they aim to complete their degrees. We also seek to highlight diverse research and speakers at key points in their career to help trainees to forge new ideas and connections.

mpu:67756.description:
OUR's mission is to:
- Guide and engage undergraduates with research at Princeton
- Unlock opportunities enhancing independent work experiences with OUR research programs, guides, and grants
- Prepare students to communicate their research and celebrate their achievements

CONTACT Princeton is a Student Volunteers Council service project and one of the College Branches of CONTACT of Mercer County. CONTACT of Mercer County is a local emotional health, crisis intervention, and suicide prevention hotline connected the 988 National Crisis Line. Volunteers answer phone and messages from the local CONTACT hotlines and the 988 Crisis Line. Volunteers will complete one semester of training on mental health, crisis intervention, and active listening. The training will be approximately 2.5 hours/week on Zoom. After the completion of training, volunteers will take at least one 4-hour shift per week, scheduled according to their availability.

mpu:67947.description:
We are a group of volunteers that work at the Princeton First Aid and Rescue Squad to serve the town of Princeton. As Emergency Medical Technicians, we work together on crews with other PFARS volunteers or paid staff to respond to 911 emergency medical calls. We provide care to sick and injured patients and transportation by ambulance to the hospital. Whether we are full-duty members or EMTs-in-training, we attend regular drills and classes to maintain our skills and ensure we provide our patients with the best care possible.
Volunteers can apply to become an EMT at PFARS. Once accepted, volunteers become junior members when they will ride on the ambulance as an assistant/shadow to two senior members. During this time, volunteers will also complete training modules (which can be done during downtime on shifts) and EMT class. After passing their junior member checkout test and the NREMT, volunteers will be promoted to senior members when they will ride on the ambulance, assisting patients alongside other senior members.
**Volunteers will receive Lyft Passes to get to and from the PFARS station. PFARS will reimburse volunteers for uniform and EMT class expenses once they pass their junior member checkout test. Options are available for students needing financial assistance.
Frequency/Time Commitment Expected
Volunteers will self-schedule shifts for 32 hours per month. Volunteers must attend the majority of monthly meetings, which are held on the second Monday of each month at 7pm. EMT class must also be completed for which there are several options. These classes typically last between 2 and 4 months for around 15 hours of class per week with additional assignments and studying to be completed independently.

We are a Student Volunteers Council (SVC) service project and Special Olympic program that serves adults with disabilities in the Princeton area. We train adult athletes in boats and on indoor rowing machines during a normal school year, and there is a large end of the year competition that we all compete in during the month of February.

SVC connects students interested in volunteering in a health care setting with the Penn Medicine Princeton Medical Center (PMPMC)'s student volunteer program. Volunteers with PMPMC commit to one weekly three-hour shift in one of the units at the Penn Medicine Princeton Medical Center (e.g. emergency room, pediatrics, neurology) and primarily work in roles that involve interacting with patients and helping the nursing staff. Duties may include: checking in with patients, translating for patients, transporting patients in wheelchairs, greeting families and visitors, organizing and stripping charts, delivering medications and lab samples, restocking rooms, answering phone calls, and more. Blood donations are crucial to improving global and community health. Our goal is to raise awareness about the importance of donating blood.
American Red Cross blood drives are held throughout the year. To prepare for the drives, students advertise physically on campus as well as digitally through list-serves and social media. Volunteers help with the campus blood drives (checking blood donors in, helping the Red Cross staff when needed, monitoring donors with snacks/drinks after donations)

mpu:68433.description:
The FFS is one of Princeton University's officially recognized Student Organizations that was launched in August 2022 with the aim of promoting French and Francophone languages and cultures among all the students (i.e. undergrads, grads, postdocs, and exchange students), regardless of their concentrations, departments, or ability to speak French. Its primary goal is to act as a forum where any Francophile student can meet, socialize, and enjoy a wide variety of events including film screenings, hangouts, guest speakers, and picnics.
This organization is open to all Princeton University graduate students interested in supporting our organization’s mission, regardless of identity, such as race, sex, ethnicity, national origin, or other protected characteristics.

mpu:68546.description: Civic Leadership Council (CLC) is part of the Pace Center for Civic Engagement and has the mission of “fostering an environment of community-building and professional skill development for Princeton students involved in civic engagement efforts through a learning experience that will enable members to act as leaders in their respective communities and future endeavors."
mpu:68546.goals: The purpose of the Council is to develop meaningful service initiatives in collaboration with community partners to address the needs of various communities. We do this by designing, planning, and implementing impactful service projects over the course of an academic year. Projects are developed by working group cohorts in diverse service areas, such as criminal justice, political engagement, health, anti-violence, and hunger and homelessness. Each cohort typically consists of a working group leader and five to eight council members.

mpu:68581.description: The Community House Executive Board advances the mission and sustainability of Community House by supporting student project leaders, strengthening program operations, and fostering meaningful collaboration with campus and community partners. Through leadership, refelction and strategic guidance, this student-led Board works to ensure that Community House programs remain responsive to community-identified needs, aligned with the organization’s values, and impactful for both students and community participants. Guided by mentorship from staff advisers and informed by community partnership and community experts, the Executive Board cultivates a strong foundation for student leadership, accountability, stweartship, innovation, and long-term community engagement.

mpu:68582.description:
Academic Success Today seeks to foster strong interpersonal relationships between Princeton students and their mentees, through tutoring, relationship-building, and academic guidance. Academic Success Today is built on 1-on-1 mentoring relationships between Princeton students and Princeton Middle School students. Princeton students enter a mentor-mentee relationship for the school year, though they are encouraged to continue with their mentee throughout their undergraduate career.
Time Commitment
Volunteers meet 2-3 times a semester for trainings, reflections, and community building.
Volunteers work with mentees weekly through direct service.

We are committed to increasing diversity in biotech, helping students build connections within the industry, and cultivating an innovative biotech community at Princeton to support academic spinouts and translational research. mpu:70041.description: PUEDO's mission is to uplift and educate the next generation of impact-oriented leaders at Princeton through service and research at nonprofits worldwide.

mpu:71303.description: Native Graduate Students of Princeton (NGSP) is a student organization that homes the Native American graduate student population at Princeton. There is not currently an organized support structure for the Native American graduate student population on campus, so this group is essential for creating community amongst us. In addition to community building, our overarching goal is to create a network through which we can amplify the voice of Natives at Princeton (the university's smallest minority population). According to demographic information provided by Inclusive Princeton "Native American, Native Hawaiian/Pacific Islander, and Native Alaskan individuals account for less than 1% of the campus population in all categories". In light of this fact, we plan to collaborate with the university about ways to better recruit and sustain a Native student body here on campus. Indeed, our group is a crucial support structure for sustaining our enrollment and ability to succeed in this university through the duration of our programs. We have already been quite active with activities on campus--we've been organizing a speaker series (with two speakers already this academic year) highlighting Native American activists, scholars, and creatives as a way of both promoting Native presence on campus and contributing to the conversation within Indigenous Studies, a field of discipline that the university still has not formally recognized at the institutional level. Indigenous Studies does not have a program, department, or center on campus, so the advocacy work NGSP will do to promote the necessity of Indigenous Studies on campus is absolutely vital. In this capacity, we will be coordinating with PAIISWG (Princeton's American Indian and Indigenous Studies Graduate Working Group) as well as NAISIP (Native American Indigenous Studies Initiative at Princeton) to organize academic events. Further, we plan to coordinate cultural events with the undergraduate group, Natives at Princeton (NAP), as a way to enhance the larger Native community on campus. Our ultimate goal is to create weekly meetings, open to both graduate and undergraduate Native students, as a way of providing a stable community for everyone at a university that, heretofore, has left Native students feeling dispersed. Other activities of note include: collaborating with NAISIP and IAS on the annual Munsee Language Symposium and the Humanities Council Land, Language, and Art Global Initiative Grant, organizing culture nights around Native foodways, crafts, stories, and planning more events across the university during Native Heritage Month.

mpu:71306.description: Our goal is to share the love and practice of ceramics! All of our workshops are suitable for beginners, and we always have someone in the studio to help you. If you already have experience in ceramics, please sign up for a workshop or open studio to learn something new or work at your own pace. We are only open to Currently Enrolled Princeton University Undergraduate Students.
mpu:71306.whatWeDo:
Members get a sense of community and early notification of ceramics studio events. You must have checked in to an event in the ceramics studio to become a member.
We provide all the tools and materials you need, and there is no charge! All we ask is that you put as much care into cleaning up and putting away tools as you do to making art!
We offer workshops in wheel-throwing, handbuilding, decorating and glazing, and you can work on functional pottery or sculpture. We ask that you respect the instructors, most of whom are students, and some of whom are volunteers, by not asking for special favors. (For example, do not ask a handbuilding instructor if you can use the wheel. Most workshops are either handbuilding OR wheel-throwing, not both).
We are only upen to current undergraduate students. Unfortunately we can not allow faculty, staff, graduate students, alumni, guests, friends, or parents, etc. to use the studio. Faculty can request academic course support by emailing reichard@princeton.edu.
Sign up for our listserve here:
https://lists.princeton.edu/cgi-bin/wa?SUBED1=CERAMICSNCW
If you have prior experience in ceramics, let us know, as we regularly hire new employees as ours graduate. Contact us at ncwceramics@princeton.edu.

mpu:71310.description:
The Brazilian Graduate Association aims to enhance the connections between Brazilian graduate students and others interested in the Brazilian culture. To achieve this purpose, we plan to promote several cultural events. First, we aim to celebrate the main Brazilian festivities such as Carnival and the Saint John’s Party. Second, we plan to organize gastronomic events, including the traditional Brazilian barbecue. Additionally, we intend to host karaoke featuring Brazilian music, with genres ranging from the widely known Samba and Bossa Nova to the less internationally renowned Forró and Sertanejo. Brazilians form an expressive community of graduate students at Princeton. However, the absence of a formal association to plan official events is a barrier to strengthening relationships among Brazilian students. Moreover, Brazil hosts amazing world-renowned festivities, and Princetonians would surely enjoy such events on campus.

mpu:71311.description:
The purpose of this club is to provide more accessible training in Muay Thai
to graduate students who are interested in the sport. Muay Thai is a martial
art that originated in Thailand and has gained popularity around the world.
It is also called the "art of eight limbs" since the boxing style involves the
use of fists, elbows, knees and shins. It is both a practical fighting style that
empowers students to defend themselves in the face of danger but also a
beautiful art rich in techniques. The Muay Thai club intends to bring
professional Muay Thai trainers on campus to teach students the
techniques and also supervise the training sessions. Since Muay Thai gyms
are typically located near Philly or New York, we think that bringing trainers
here on campus can make the sport more readily accessible to graduate students.

mpu:71315.description:

These include an active seminar series, an annual research workshop, policy meetings, public commentary, visiting fellows, graduate and undergraduate student activities, a Senior Thesis prize, and formal partnerships with Humboldt University, Sciences Po, and the University of Geneva.
Founded in 2004, the program is directed by Andrew Moravcsik and Sophie Meunier. The EU Program welcomes proposals for collaboration from students, scholars and fellows. mpu:71320.description:

The Progressive Law Society is an undergraduate chapter of the American Constitution Society (ACS), America’s leading progressive legal advocacy organization. Princeton joins an expansive network of law school and lawyer chapters who share in our mission to ensure that the fundamental principles of human dignity, individual rights and liberties, genuine equality, and access to justice are in their rightful, central place in American law.
The Progressive Law Society invites all Princeton undergraduates, graduates, faculty, staff, and community members to enjoy our public lectures and programming.

By fostering critical thinking, visual literacy, dialogue, and empathy, the Museum aspires to enrich human experience and to strengthen citizenship.
The Princeton University Art Museum educates, challenges, and inspires the students of Princeton University and members of a diverse local, national, and international public through exposure to the world of art. Uniting fresh, object-based scholarship with broad accessibility, the Museum soothes and provokes, affirms accepted meanings and suggests new ones, excites the imagination, and affords encounters of both clarity and uncertainty. Intimate in scale yet expansive in scope, the Museum presents opportunities to delve deeply into the study of art and culture, offers a revitalizing experience of extraordinary works of art, and acts as a library of the visual and a gateway to the University’s intellectual resources.

mpu:71359.description:
Princeton Collegiate Moot Court (PCMC) is Princeton University’s premier moot court team, competing against peer universities in simulated appellate arguments before panels of legal faculty, practitioners, and distinguished jurists. Founded in late 2022 and entirely student-run, PCMC participates at an elite level in both written and oral advocacy through the American Moot Court Association (AMCA).
Each year, AMCA releases an original fact pattern with two unresolved legal issues based on real case law, forming the basis for that year’s oral and written competitions. PCMC members read legal precedents and develop arguments in support of either the petitioner or respondent. PCMC affords its members the opportunity to develop critical writing, logic, and legal reasoning skills. Participants also have the opportunity to hone their appellate advocacy skill by thinking and responding extemporaneously to sophisticated legal questions.
PCMC hosts tryouts each fall to select new members.

mpu:71363.description:
Hi, we’re OCE!
We create shared experiences for all undergrads, grads, faculty, and staff to step away from their day-to-day routine and explore opportunities that promote connection and growth beyond the resume.
We are pro-participation; perfection is not required.
We aspire…
to cultivate a Princeton campus culture that values sharing the varied passions and experiences of our community in ways that transcend roles, hierarchies, and disciplines.
mpu:71363.goals:
1. We believe that everyone on campus has skills and knowledge to share with others.
2. We believe that joy and fun matter and should be cultivated.
3. We promote growth beyond the resume and focus on optional, low-pressure engagement.
4. We prioritize and seek to contribute to the mental, social and emotional wellbeing of the Princeton community.
5. Though undergraduate and graduate student community-building, learning, teaching and enrichment is the central focus of OCE, we welcome our whole University community to participate.
6. We prioritize quality over quantity when it comes to our programming decisions.
7. Inclusion, equity and universal design are all foundational to how we design and approach our work.
8. We seek out sustainable sourcing for OCE’s food and materials.
9. We encourage and model respect for the time and effort of those who help to lead our programming, including, but not limited to, OCE staff, Wintersession facilitators, Princeton Research Day presenters, peer to peer educators, campus partners and local community members.
10. We recognize that personal growth and fulfillment can come from trying new and unexpected activities.
We strive to make experimentation, exploration, and connection the goal of engagement, rather than productivity.

. Hosting regular discussions focused on trainee research-related topics to cultivate an active local community.

mpu:71375.tagline: Human-AI Interaction and Ethics Community at Princeton
mpu:71375.description:
Empowering Tomorrow's Human-AI Interaction & Ethics Community
ETHICOM is dedicated to bringing together and empowering tomorrow's leaders in the field of Human-AI Interaction and Ethics. Our purpose is to foster a vibrant community that explores, discusses, and advances the ethical dimensions of artificial intelligence to ensure a responsible and inclusive future. Through interdisciplinary collaboration, discussions, and engaging activities, we bridge academia, industry, and society. Our community learns about AI's impact, how to advocate for bias-free algorithms, and how to cultivate responsible human-AI relationships. We envision an AI future guided by diversity, fairness, transparency, and human-centric design.
ETHICOM prioritizes practical application by providing valuable opportunities for our members. We offer a comprehensive wintersession course on AI ethics, allowing participants to delve into the intricacies of ethical considerations in AI. Additionally, we organize engaging debates with industry experts, where we explore real-world ethics processes and gain insights from professionals in the field. We actively promote awareness of and involvement in Princeton's existing AI-ethics opportunities, ranging from interactive reading clubs to in-depth case studies. Through these activities, we foster a community that is well-informed and actively engaged in the ethical aspects of AI. Furthermore, we recognize the importance of networking and career development in the realm of AI ethics. By connecting our members with professionals and providing relevant development opportunities, we equip them with the necessary tools and connections to pursue impactful careers in the field.
Join us in shaping an ethical and inclusive AI landscape. Together, we empower the next generation of leaders both within and beyond Princeton to make meaningful contributions, drive responsible innovation, and align AI development with society's best interests.

The Center is committed to the study of religion through diverse methods across historical and contemporary manifestations, and to the dissemination of the fruits of religion scholarship to the Princeton campus and broader public. It aims to facilitate understanding of religion through an integrated program of support for Princeton faculty to pursue research, teaching, and scholarly engagement; awards for Princeton graduate students to pursue dissertation research and undergraduate students to prepare independent work; interdisciplinary seminars and colloquia; courses; public lectures and conferences; opportunities for visiting scholars to affiliate with the Center; and a growing library of publicly-available digital media.

3. Professional Development: Access unique opportunities such as workshops, seminars, and partnerships like the CariScholar initiative, enhancing your academic and career trajectories.
4. Cultural Exposure: Attend events showcasing Caribbean music, dance, cuisine, and traditions, enriching your cultural palette and appreciation.
5. Support System: Find a tight-knit community ready to offer emotional and academic support, mentorship, and guidance throughout your graduate journey.
6. Leadership Opportunities: Take on roles within the association to hone your leadership, organizational, and management skills.
7. Discussion Forums: Engage in meaningful discussions on Caribbean socio-economic, political, and cultural topics, broadening your understanding and perspective.
8. Social Events: Enjoy get-togethers, celebrations, and other social events, providing a break from academic rigor and fostering friendships.
9. Inclusivity: Benefit from an environment that emphasizes diversity, inclusivity, and mutual respect, promoting personal growth.
10. Advocacy: Be part of a collective voice advocating for the needs and concerns of Caribbean students within the larger academic community.

The mission of the Princeton Libations Association (PLA) is to introduce graduate students to the history, science, and cultural contexts of diverse culinary traditions in a congenial and welcoming environment.
PLA events typically involve professional and student-led tastings, demonstrations, and cooking workshops. Sessions themes include tastings of various varieties of wine, beer, non-alcoholic beverages (like kombucha or coffee), and foods (like hard cheeses or cured meats). The PLA also sponsors demonstrations and workshops on cooking skills (like pizza-making, charcuterie-plating, or beer brewing).
In addition to its regular programming, the PLA encourages graduate students to propose and lead sessions based on their own culinary interests. In doing so, the organization hopes to highlight culinary traditions representative of and led by students from a variety of cultural backgrounds. Please email amhoyt@princeton.edu with any questions or to propose an event.

mpu:71451.description:
National Alzheimer’s Buddies is an intergenerational movement responding to the profound isolation and social disengagement experienced by people in the intermediate-to-late stages of Alzheimer’s disease (AD). Through partnering college volunteers with residents (buddies) at memory care facilities, we build meaningful, lasting relationships that break through the boundaries imposed by Alzheimer’s disease. Learn more at our instagram @alzbuddies_princeton
A central focus of Alzheimer’s Buddies is building meaningful relationships between volunteers, dementia residents, and staff/nurses. These relationships are cultivated with weekly 2 hour long volunteering sessions at the Senior Living Center and monthly reflection meetings among volunteers. During weekly volunteering, volunteers travel together to the facility and engage in a variety of activities such as arts and crafts, chair exercises, or cognitive memory games with the residents. Alzheimer’s Buddies encourages students to take the mindset of a friend rather than of a care provider, to learn about their patients' past and passions, and to establish real friendships with individuals in the broader Princeton community.
Frequency/Time Commitment Expected: 2 hrs/wk volunteer session + 1 hr/month reflection meeting
Mode of communication: Email, Groupme

Due to onboarding requirements necessitated by the senior living facilities and National Alzheimer's Buddies association, we currently have only 2 time points during which applications are open to join Princeton Alzheimer's Buddies as a volunteer. We post the link to applications on the residential college Listservs and send the link to anyone who has filled out the interest form at the activities fair OR reached out to us via email. Our application process involves a written application and coffee chat, which are evaluated by separate board members. mpu:71478.tagline: We are the Student Wing for Solidaridad Central Jersey, a Pro Se Clinic that helps empower recent immigrants seeking asylum and legal status by providing assistance in filing their applications for asylum and work permits.
mpu:71478.description:
Volunteers with the Solidaridad Pro Se Clinic are committed to the fight for and advancement of immigrant rights in collaboration with Solidaridad Central Jersey. Volunteers will be tasked with supporting the mission and efforts of Solidaridad mainly through research and writing skills. Tasks will depend on the needs of the community partner, emphasizing our personalized approach. As an example, volunteers have previously assisted with note-taking and interpretation to help asylum seekers—who we call “neighbors”–complete their applications for asylum or drafting country condition indexes on locations where many asylum seekers originated. These reports assist Solidaridad in their compilation of supporting documents in asylum applications.
In the past, the first few meetings of the Solidaridad Student Wing were focused around volunteer recruitment, and during following meetings, members of the Solidaridad join the second session to explain Solidaridad’s work. Students who are interested in becoming volunteers can sign up for Solidaridad’s volunteer training session. Due to ongoing developments in the immigration landscape, there is less of a need for student volunteers to assist with asylum applications; however, the perspective and energy of young advocates is essential to Solidaridad’s mission, and the organization is in need of volunteers who can support its dynamic approach to helping our neighbors.
Members of the Solidaridad Student Wing can choose from a variety of tasks to help Solidaridad:
- Carrying out admin tasks in the Solidaridad office which is at a 10 minute walk from campus (printing/copying/scanning applications, following up with work permits, other assignments as needed)
- Serving as mentors for new student volunteers, answering questions, checking in during their shadowing period, and providing advice/support when a new student is assigned to a team
- Serving as interpreters or note-takers for asylum applications
- Drafting policy briefs on updates to immigration policy and processes
- Creating materials for asylum seekers, such as information videos and documents
For fluent Spanish speakers who do not have enough time to commit to working on a single case weekly for about a month, there are short-term, single-session activities they could choose from:
- Acting as interpreters to complete the demographics pages of I-589
- Translating Spanish documents into English to supplement asylum applications
In addition to deepening connections to asylum seekers, the group will also deepen connections with a community organization in Princeton. The group will also strengthen the community within Princeton’s student body, allowing for students to come together through a passion for immigrant rights. It will create a space dedicated to doing social good and living in alignment with one’s values, and it will create a space dedicated to raising awareness about current immigration events on campus.
Frequency/Time Commitment Expected
The student wing will meet for an hour each week to complete tasks set by Solidaridad. Some members may also choose to join the Solidaridad Pro Se Clinic as volunteers, which would be a separate time commitment.

mpu:71608.description: The Negative Capability Collective is a gathering of readers, writers, critics, and lovers of poetry. Practices on handbells twice weekly; travel to New York to ring tower bells at Trinity Church 2-4 times per month.
Change-ringing is the centuries-old English folk tradition of ringing mathematical permutations of tuned bells. While a fascinating combination of math and music, change-ringing does not require any background in math or music to appreciate; its practice is a fun challenge for the mind, an interesting tune for the ears, and even akin to meditation after enough practice. The Change-Ringers practice change-ringing on University-purchased handbells and plan two practices a week, in addition to frequent travel to NYC's Trinity Church for tower bell ringing. Interested members may partake in a short performance once in a while. All beginners welcome. (If you've heard of change-ringing before Princeton, I'll be impressed.)

mpu:71695.description:
The SUCCEED Program at Trenton Central High School empowers Princeton University students to support high school students as they work to strengthen their academic performance, build essential learning skills, and pursue their aspirations of attending four-year colleges. In partnership with Trenton Central High School, volunteers provide consistent tutoring and mentoring support focused on homework, classwork, and core academic concepts, while also helping students develop foundational skills such as time management, note-taking, writing, and study strategies.
Rooted in the SUCCEED framework—Set Goals, Utilize your skills, Communicate your needs, Create healthy habits, Evaluate your materials, Execute your goals, and Determine the student you want to be—the program encourages students to take ownership of their academic journey and long-term success. Princeton student mentors work alongside school professionals and community educators, gaining hands-on experience in youth development, academic coaching, and relationship-building while learning directly from experts in secondary education. Through this collaborative model, SUCCEED fosters confidence, accountability, and opportunity for students while cultivating meaningful leadership and service experiences for university volunteers.

mpu:71719.description:
The Community-Based Tutoring-Mentoring (CBT) Matching Program is run through the Pace Center's Community House with a focus on supporting middle and high school students in the Princeton community to overcome the education gap. The goal of the program is to match Princeton University volunteers with middle and high school students in the Princeton community so the volunteer can act as a resource for the student, whether they're looking for academic support, advice in college/career exploration, or general mentorship.
